> AGENT

I've now got a full picture across the game's systems, world simulation, and release history. Here's my honest read.

## Where the game actually is

It's gone remarkably **deep on player-facing systems** — 7 gear tiers, enchant/brew/anvil/grindstone/mending, XP, 4 game modes × 4 difficulties + hardcore, armor with body rendering, and now advancements & statistics. On the "things a player *does*" axis, you're close to Minecraft parity.

But the **world itself is comparatively static and lonely**:
- Mobs never despawn and never react to each other — they wander, aggro you, flee you, and that's it. No herds, no predator/prey, no day/night routines.
- Biomes are purely *visual* — identical ores, mobs, and trees everywhere.
- Weather is cosmetic only — rain/snow change the sky and audio but touch nothing in the sim.
- Villagers wander among generated "houses," but there are **no real settlements** — a gap your own roadmap has deferred *twice*.
- Beyond breeding and footstep particles, there's no ambient life.

## What I think about "Living World"

It's the **right frontier** — your instinct is good. The systems are rich; the world is quiet, and that's the most valuable thing left to fix. Worth noting: you already shipped *layer one* of this (cosmetic weather, ambient mob sounds, day/night mob behavior, breeding). So "Living World" here isn't net-new — it's making that layer **reactive and inhabited**.

The catch: "Living World" is a *theme*, not one feature. Here's how I'd slice it, building on `mobAI.ts`, `spawnDirector.ts`, `breeding.ts`, `randomTicks.ts`, and `weather.ts`:

1. **Ambient wildlife** — birds, fireflies, fish schools, cave bats as cheap transient cosmetic entities. Biggest "alive" payoff per line; zero save/worldgen risk.
2. **Mob ecology & routines** — herd/flock cohesion, animals bedding at night, passives fleeing *hostiles* (not just you), distance-based despawn so the population breathes.
3. **Wandering trader / roaming events** — a periodic traveling merchant (reuses your villager trade pipeline), maybe a horde night. Gives the world a pulse.
4. **Weather with consequences** — rain slows/douses, thunderstorms boost spawns or charge creepers. Turns cosmetic weather into a mechanic.
5. **Villages** *(the ambitious one)* — clustered generated settlements. Highest impact, but the **only slice needing a `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump** (invalidates existing worlds — you've done this for coal/lava, so it's precedented, not free).

**My recommendation:** ship Living World in two passes. Do **1–4 first** — all entity/behavior-level, no worldgen bump, low save risk, and they deliver the "world is alive" feeling immediately. Treat **Villages** as a dedicated follow-up. Don't bundle them — the risk profiles are completely different.

Let me confirm the direction before I design the plan.

- **Scope of any option** — e.g. exactly which sub-slices "Pass 1" would include, or what a Village would contain.

What's on your mind?

> DEVELOPER

I am thinking Generated villages + villager professions + raids, plus tameable wolf/cat companions that fight for me. what do you think?

> AGENT

I think it's a **strong, coherent vision** — and notably, it's not a grab-bag. The four pieces reinforce each other:

- **Villages** give raids something to attack and companions a world worth defending.
- **Professions** make a village worth caring about (and protecting in a raid).
- **Raids** turn villages from scenery into stakes.
- **Companions** are the thing that helps you *survive* a raid.

That synergy is exactly what makes a "Living World" update feel like an *update* and not four loose additions. It's essentially Minecraft's best content update (Village & Pillage) plus the most-loved companion mobs. I'm into it.

Now the honest part — two things nobody's mentioned yet that will shape everything:

**1. The hidden foundation: mob persistence.** Right now **no mobs are saved at all** — every creature is a session-only entity that respawns from scratch on reload. That's invisible today, but it breaks three of your four features:
- A tamed wolf that vanishes when you reload would feel *broken*, not charming.
- A village librarian whose profession and trades reshuffle every load isn't a village resident — it's a slot machine.
- Mid-raid reloads would lose the raid.

So the real first task isn't villages — it's a **mob-persistence layer** (a save-format bump + serialization). The minimal version: persist only *tamed pets* and *village residents*; leave the wild wandering population transient as it is now.

**2. The second shared prerequisite: mob-vs-mob combat.** Today the AI is strictly binary — passives flee *you*, hostiles attack *you*. Nothing fights anything else. But your wolf attacking a zombie, and a raider attacking a villager, are the *same new capability*: a third allegiance and target-selection among mobs. Build it once → both raids and companions use it. Nice consolidation.

**Everything else is well-supported by what's already there:** professions ride your existing villager-trade pipeline (`trades.ts` → station-recipes); raids reuse the boss wave/minion-summon pattern in `mobAI.ts`; new mobs (raider/wolf/cat) follow the established exhaustive-`MobKind` + procedural-model convention (zero assets holds). Villages are the one piece needing a `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump (precedented — coal/lava did it; it invalidates existing worlds of the current version).

**The catch is size.** This is realistically a **3–4 PR epic** — roughly a whole release's worth of work, not one feature. So the real question is sequencing. Dependency-wise, raids *can't* go first (they need a village to defend), and companions are the most self-contained. My instinct: prove out the persistence + ally-AI foundation inside the smallest, most delightful slice (companions), then build outward to villages → professions → raids.

825	    state.mobs.splice(index, 1);
826	    // Babies drop nothing — only grown animals yield loot. `lootingLevel` is the
827	    // *killing* melee weapon's Looting (forwarded by tryAttackMob); indirect kills
828	    // (arrows, thrown spears, explosions) pass 0, since Looting is a melee enchant.
829	    const drops = mob.ageTimer <= 0 ? rollMobDrops(mob.kind, this.rng, lootingLevel) : [];

832	    }

840	      state.victory = true;

849	   */

851	    const state = this.state;
852	    const slot = state.inventory[state.selectedSlot];

854	    if (state.mobs.some((mob) => mob.kind === "boss")) {

860	    state.inventory = inv.adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, "boss_summoner", -1, state.selectedSlot) ?? state.inventory;
861	    this.emit({ type: "bossSummoned", x: point.x, y: point.y, z: point.z });
862	    return true;
863	  }
864	
865	  private get mobTickDeps() {
866	    return {
867	      surfaceYAt: this.surfaceYAt,
868	      applyDamage: this.applyDamage,
869	      removeMobAt: this.removeMobAt,
870	      rng: this.rng,
871	      emit: this.emit
872	    };
873	  }

Honestly? For the **whole 5-phase epic**, one PR is too much — but you're right that five is probably too many. Let me explain the trade-off, because there's a clean middle.

**Why one PR for everything worries me:**
- It stacks **two save migrations (v13→v14→v15) and a world-invalidating worldgen bump (8→9)** into a single all-or-nothing merge. You couldn't ship companions without also shipping raids.
- The diff would be huge — a new mob-persistence serialization layer, worldgen structure generation + a hash re-baseline, **three** new mob kinds across six tables each, the raid system, and professions/trades. CodeRabbit and a human both review large diffs worse.
- If review finds a problem in raids or villages, your already-solid companion work is held hostage.
- Your own AGENTS.md frames a branch as landing "one reviewable unit" — a 5-phase epic is really five.

**Why five PRs is overkill:** the phases share so much foundation that splitting every one adds ceremony without isolating much.

**What I'd actually do — two PRs**, each one cohesive risk class, each with several focused commits (your usual style):

- **PR-A — "Living mobs & companions"** (Phase 0b + persistence + companions): pure behavior + save `v13→v14`, **no worldgen bump**. Allegiance/mob-vs-mob, mob persistence, tameable wolf/cat. Self-contained and low-risk.
- **PR-B — "Villages, professions & raids"** (Phases 2–4): the settlement cluster — worldgen `8→9` (the world-invalidating change, quarantined here), save `v14→v15`, raider mob + raids.

This honors your "few PRs, several commits" instinct (two, not five), keeps each review tractable, and crucially isolates the one change that throws away existing worlds. Within each PR, one commit per slice, lint green at every commit.

If you'd still rather do a single PR, I'd at least scope it to **PR-A only** and treat villages/raids as a follow-up — never the full epic in one merge.

Which delivery structure do you want? I'll update the roadmap in the plan accordingly.

# Living World — phased feature epic

## Context

The game has gone **deep on player-facing systems** (7 gear tiers, enchant/brew/anvil/grindstone/mending, XP, 4 game modes × 4 difficulties + hardcore, armor, advancements & stats) but the **world itself is static and lonely**: mobs never react to each other, biomes are visual-only, weather is cosmetic, villagers wander among generated "houses" with no real settlements, and *no mob is ever saved* (every creature is session-only, respawned from scratch each boot).

The user wants a **"Living World"** direction built from four reinforcing pieces — **generated villages + villager professions + raids + tameable wolf/cat companions that fight for the player** (essentially Minecraft's Village & Pillage + companion mobs). The pieces synergize: villages give raids a target, professions make villages worth defending, raids turn villages into stakes, companions help you survive.

This is a large epic resting on two shared, currently-missing prerequisites: **mob persistence** and **mob-vs-mob combat (a third allegiance)**. The user chose to plan the whole arc now and ship it as **two PRs** (see Roadmap) — Phase 1 execution-ready, later phases sketched. **PR-A is authorized to push + open; PR-B is built locally and held for the user's review before any push.**

All design claims below were verified against source. Project constraints hold throughout: **zero binary assets** (procedural models/sprites, ZZFX audio), one logical commit per slice, Conventional Commits, docs+tests+CHANGELOG ship *with* each change, and the full verify gate green before anything lands.

## Roadmap at a glance

**Delivery: two branches → two PRs, each with focused commits (one per slice), gate green at every commit.**

| PR | Branch | Commits (phase) | Save | Worldgen | Push? |

| **PR-A — Living mobs & companions** | `feat/living-mobs-companions` | c1 allegiance + mob-vs-mob (0b) · c2 mob persistence (0a) · c3 wolf/cat: tame/sit/follow/fight (1) · c4 docs/CHANGELOG | **v13→v14** | none | **Yes — push + open PR (authorized)** |
| **PR-B — Villages, professions & raids** | `feat/villages-professions-raids` | c1 generated villages (2) · c2 villager professions (3) · c3 raids (4) · c4 docs/CHANGELOG | **v14→v15** | **8→9** | **No — build locally, hold for user review before push** |

PR-A carries no worldgen change; **PR-B quarantines the world-invalidating `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9 bump**. PR-B branches off PR-A's merged `main` (it depends on PR-A's v14 `mobs` persistence field for village residents) — so **PR-A merges first, then PR-B**.

**Commit/phase order = dependency order** within and across PRs: 0b → 0a → 1 (PR-A), then 2 → 3 → 4 (PR-B). Persistence (PR-A c2) must precede companions and residents; villages (PR-B c1) must precede professions and raids. **Tests ship inside each feature commit** (mandatory to keep the gate green per-commit); **docs + CHANGELOG consolidate in each PR's final commit** along with that PR's e2e save/worldgen-version assert bump.

Two technical limits accepted for this epic: **mob-vs-mob is melee-only** (the `ProjectileState.fromPlayer` filter is binary — `state.ts:72` — so mob arrows can only hit the player; team-aware projectiles are a separate effort), and **difficulty `dmgScale` applies only to damage dealt *to the player*** (mob-vs-mob uses raw `attackDamage`).

## PR-A · c1 — Phase 0b: Allegiance + mob-vs-mob combat (no save bump)

**Allegiance model** (`lib/game/engine/state.ts`, `MobState` at line 29). Keep `hostile: boolean` (load-bearing for caps, `despawnHostiles`, snapshot counts, health-bar gate). Add a coexisting targeting axis:
- `faction: "wild" | "hostile" | "ally" | "villager" | "raider"` — set at spawn from a `FACTION_BY_KIND` map.
- `owner?: "player"` — pet ownership (define now so the persisted shape is stable; used in PR2).
- `targetId: number | null` + `retargetTimer: number` — session-only targeting cache/throttle.

Initial mapping: sheep/chicken/horse/cow/pig→`wild`; zombie/skeleton/spider/creeper/boss→`hostile`; villager→`villager`. `pushMob` (`spawnDirector.ts:32`) sets `faction` from the map; `spawnBaby` (`breeding.ts:52`) inherits parent `faction`/`owner`.

**Shared targeting** (`lib/game/engine/systems/mobAI.ts`). One pure helper `selectMobTarget(state, mob)` driven by an enmity table (`ally→{hostile,raider}`, `hostile→{villager,ally}`, `raider→{villager,ally}`, `wild`/`villager`→∅). Only fighter factions scan; a fighter rescans only when `retargetTimer ≤ 0` or its cached target is dead/out-of-range, then one linear nearest-enemy pass reusing existing scratch vectors. Throttle to `MOB_RETARGET_SECONDS` (~0.6s) so steering stays O(N)/frame and scans amortize to ~1–2 Hz per fighter (safe for the ~70-mob population). **Preserve player aggro exactly as today** — a `hostile` prefers the player when in range (existing `activeHostile` block), falling through to a mob target only otherwise (keeps every existing test green). Villagers/`wild` never fight; villagers gain a *flee-from-nearest-enemy* branch mirroring the animal-flee branch at `mobAI.ts:166`.

**Striking a mob target.** In melee reach + LOS with `attackTimer ≤ 0`: lower `target.hp`, apply knockback (same `addScaledVector` pattern as `tryAttackMob`, `combat.ts:89`), emit `mobAttacked`, reset timer. Deaths still handled only by the existing post-loop sweep (`mobAI.ts:277`) — never mid-loop (splice-safety invariant).

**Kill credit** (`removeMobAt`, `GameEngine.ts:822`). Current signature `removeMobAt(index, lootingLevel = 0)` routes drops→`state.inventory` and XP→`awardXp` (player), hard-coding player credit. Generalize to `removeMobAt(index, opts?: { credit?: boolean; lootingLevel?: number })`, `credit` defaulting `true` so **all existing call sites are unchanged**. The death sweep computes credit from the **victim's faction**: `credit = victim.faction ∈ {wild, hostile, raider}` (false for `ally`/`villager`). Rationale: a pet killing a hostile *should* feed your inventory/XP ("your wolf hunts for you"); a slain villager/pet yields nothing, and this closes the XP-leak where mobs killing each other would farm player XP. Boss-victory branch (`kind === "boss"`) untouched.

**Save/worldgen:** none (new fields session-only). **Tests** (`mobAI.test.ts`): zombie-next-to-villager engagement; the enmity table + `selectMobTarget` as pure units; credit rule (hostile death credits player, villager death does not); existing dawn-aggro regressions stay green. **Docs:** `architecture.md` (allegiance + `removeMobAt` credit opt), `adding-content.md` (`faction` + enmity table), `testing.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## PR-A · c2–c3 — Phase 0a + 1: Mob persistence + companions (save v13→v14)

### Mob persistence (Phase 0a)

`SavedMob = { kind, x, y, z, hp, faction, owner?, sitting?, ageTimer? }`. Re-derive everything else (`speed`, `detectRange`, `attackDamage`, `halfHeight`, fresh `direction`/`yaw`/`bobSeed`/timers) from `MOB_TEMPLATES`. Never persist `fedTimer`/`summonTimer`/`fuseTimer`/`targetId`/`id`.

**Policy: persist only the `persistent` set — `isPersistentMob(m) = m.owner != null || m.faction === "villager"`** (tamed pets ∪ village residents), NOT the whole population. Justification: ambient wildlife/hostiles are fungible (`spawnInitialMobs` re-seeds them every boot, so persisting would *double* them), it bounds save size, and boss/creepers are already deliberately transient. In PR2 only pets match; PR3 residents match automatically.

`serializeMobs`/`restoreMobs` in `lib/game/save.ts` (mirror `serializeContainers`/`readContainers`): serialize filters `isPersistentMob`; restore validates each entry, rebuilds a full `MobState` via the template factory, **re-grounds y** via `surfaceYAt(x,z)+halfHeight` (handles pets saved on now-air/buried terrain), clamps/drops out-of-bounds, and assigns **fresh sequential ids** (safe — renderer reconciles by id from a cold boot). `migrateSaveV13toV14` is a pure bump (`mobs` absent ⇒ empty); add `if (migrated.version === 13) … = migrateSaveV13toV14(...)` and accept `version === 14`. **Wiring** (`GameEngine.ts` ctor, ~line 286): restore persisted mobs **before** `spawnInitialMobs` (which still runs unconditionally to seed fungible mobs); `serialize()` adds `mobs: serializeMobs(state.mobs)`. Caps only gate breeding/night spawns, so a few extra restored mobs self-limit — no crash/runaway. **Renderer re-attach:** none needed (`mobVisuals.sync` auto-creates models for unseen ids; pets non-hostile ⇒ no health bar).

### Companions (Phase 1)

**New `MobKind`s `wolf` + `cat`** — fill all **six** exhaustive tables (the Plan agent corrected the count from five): `MOB_TEMPLATES` (`mobs.ts`), `MOB_DROPS` (`mobLoot.ts`, both `[]`), `MOB_XP` (`mobXp.ts`), `CALL_INTERVALS` (`audio/mobAmbience.ts`), `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS` + `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS` (`audio/soundParams.ts`); neither joins `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS`. Wolf: grey body, `hp 8`, `attackDamage 4`, `detectRange 0` while wild. Cat: orange tabby, `attackDamage 3`. On tame, raise hp to `PET_TAMED_HP` and set `detectRange = PET_FIGHT_RANGE`.

**Taming** reuses the feed plumbing in `lib/game/engine/systems/interact.ts`. `TAME_ITEMS = { wolf: "bone", cat: "raw_fish" }` (both items already exist — `items.ts:123,166`). `tryTameAimedMob` mirrors `tryFeedAimedMob` (`findAimedMobIndex` + `adjustSlotCount`): on a wild wolf/cat roll `TAME_CHANCE` (~1/3); on success set `owner:"player"`, `faction:"ally"`, raise hp/detectRange, emit `mobTamed`. `tryToggleSitPet` flips `sitting` on your own pet (emit `petSitToggled`).

**Right-click precedence** (`dispatch`, ~`GameEngine.ts:538`): `throw spear → tryTameAimedMob (wild pet + bone/fish) → tryToggleSitPet (own pet, non-food hand) → tryFeedAimedMob (breeding) → tryTradeAimedVillager → tryInteractBlock → trySummonBoss → tryFish → tryUseHeldItem → place`.

**Ally state machine** (`mobAI.ts`, `faction === "ally"` branch): `sitting` ⇒ fully parked; else valid enemy in range ⇒ engage+melee (credit-true kills feed the player via PR1's rule); else owner distance `> PET_FOLLOW_MAX` (~10) ⇒ steer to owner, `> PET_TELEPORT_DISTANCE` (~24) ⇒ teleport adjacent on solid ground; else gentle wander near owner.

**Breeding/drops:** add wolf/cat to `FEED_ITEMS`, gate pet breeding on `owner` set; `spawnBaby` inherits `faction`+`owner` so juveniles are owned allies (and persist). **Renderer:** wolf/cat via existing `createMobModel` `modelArgs` (no new geometry); optional cheap reads of `MobState` — red collar tint when `owner != null`, sit pose when `sitting`. **Events/audio:** add `mobTamed`/`petSitToggled` to `GameEvent` (`state.ts`), route in `audioDirector.ts`, add a heart-burst case in `particleSystem.ts`.

**Save/worldgen:** save **v13→v14** (additive `mobs?`), worldgen stays **8**. **Tests:** `save.test.ts` (migration; round-trip; unknown-kind/garbage-hp/non-finite dropping); `GameEngine.test.ts` (tame via seeded rng; sit toggle; follow/teleport; pet kills zombie → player gets loot/XP; pet never targets player; persistence round-trip through a second engine with no wildlife duplication); `breeding.test.ts` (inheritance); exhaustive-table tests auto-extend; `mobVisuals.test.ts` (models build+dispose). **Manual pass** (not headless): wolf/cat look, collar tint, sit pose, ZZFX bark/meow, tame hearts. **Docs:** `save-format.md` (v14: `SavedMob`, persist-vs-transient policy, edge cases), `architecture.md`, `adding-content.md` (taming subsection; fix table count to six), `testing.md`, `tuning.md` (`TAME_CHANCE`, `PET_*`, `MOB_RETARGET_SECONDS`), `manual.md`/`reference.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## PR-B · c1 — Phase 2: Generated villages (worldgen 8→9) — sketch

Append `placeVillages(world, cfg)` **last** in `generateWorld` (`generation.ts`, after `placeDungeons`), driven by a dedicated `villageRand(world.seed)` (like `coalRand`/`dungeonRand`) so existing ore/tree/house/dungeon bytes stay byte-identical. Reuse `placeHouse` + existing blocks (cobblestone paths, planks, doors) arranged around a flat validated center (validate via seed-pure `terrainTopY`, keep clear of spawn) — **no new `BlockId`**. Add a `collectVillageSites` derive pass (the `collectDungeonSites` write/record-toggle pattern); engine stores session `state.villageSites` and spawns `villagersPerVillage` residents there at boot, flagged persistent (`faction === "villager"` already qualifies). **Bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9**, re-baseline `generation.test.ts` SHA-256 digests + meshing snapshot in the same commit (existing worlds discard stale diffs and reboot from seed — precedented), add a structural probe test that survives re-baselining. Residents reuse v14 — no new save bump. **Docs:** `save-format.md` (8→9), `architecture.md`, `adding-content.md`, `testing.md`, `tuning.md`, `manual.md`/`reference.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## PR-B · c2 — Phase 3: Villager professions (save v14→v15) — sketch

`Profession = "farmer"|"blacksmith"|"librarian"|"cleric"|"none"`, optional `profession?` on `MobState` (villager-only), assigned per resident at village spawn (seeded round-robin). Tag trades via a parallel `TRADE_PROFESSION: Record<recipeId, Profession>` in `trades.ts` (leave shared `Recipe` untouched). `tryTradeAimedVillager` sets `state.craftingStation = "villager"` + a session `state.activeVillagerProfession`; the Trading recipe-book category filters to it; the `craft` station gate (`GameEngine.ts:404`) adds a profession spoof-guard. **Look:** per-instance recolor of the villager smock material in `mobVisuals` (the `setPlayerSkin` in-place recolor technique) — zero assets. **Save v14→v15** (additive `profession?` on `SavedMob`, pure `migrateSaveV14toV15`, validated on load); no worldgen change. **Docs:** `save-format.md` (v15), `architecture.md`/`adding-content.md`, `testing.md`, `manual.md`/`reference.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## PR-B · c3 — Phase 4: Raids (additive item only) — sketch

**New `MobKind` `raider`** (`faction:"raider"`, `hostile:true` so it counts against `HOSTILE_CAP` and Peaceful's `despawnHostiles` clears it) — fill the six tables + `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS`; melee (per the ranged-scope limit); target priority villagers→allies→player. **Trigger** via a craftable additive **"Ominous Horn"** item, used at a village — mirrors `trySummonBoss` (`GameEngine.ts:850`) as a `placeBlock`-precedence step (`tryStartRaid`), refusing if a raid is active. **Waves** in a new `systems/raid.ts` ticked after the spawn directors, reusing `tickBossSummon`'s cap/cadence guard; session-only `state.raid: { center, wave, totalWaves, raidersAlive, timer } | null` (transient like `state.victory`). Win = all waves cleared (`raidWon` + emeralds/XP reward, optional "Hero of the Village" buff via the status-effect system); lose = all residents dead (`raidLost`); Peaceful cancels cleanly. **Save/worldgen:** none beyond the additive item id (raiders + `state.raid` transient, like the boss — reload cancels an in-progress raid). **Docs:** `architecture.md` (raid system), `adding-content.md`, `testing.md`, `tuning.md` (`RAID_WAVE_SIZE`/`RAID_WAVE_COUNT`/rewards), `manual.md`/`reference.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Cross-phase risks

- **`faction` vs `hostile`:** keep both — `hostile` stays the cap/threat/health-bar axis; `faction` adds targeting. Raiders are `hostile:true` so Peaceful clears them; ensure `state.raid` clears with them.
- **Targeting cost:** `retargetTimer` throttle keeps scans ~1–2 Hz per fighter; steering stays O(N).
- **Melee-only mob-vs-mob** and **player-only difficulty scaling** are deliberate scope limits this epic.
- **Persistence ordering:** PR-A's v14 `mobs` field must land before PR-B's village residents rely on it — **PR-A merges to `main` first, then PR-B branches off it**.
- **Worldgen 8→9 (PR-B)** discards existing worlds' block-diffs (reboot from seed) — acceptable/documented; re-baseline hashes carefully since only `villageRand` bytes change.

## Verification & delivery (the AGENTS.md gate)

Keep `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build` green **at every commit** (bisectable branch); run `bun run test:e2e` before each PR (both touch the renderer/input/shell — PR-A's e2e save-version assert bumps to v14, PR-B's to v15 + worldgen 9). Each feature commit adds the headless tests listed above; do **one consolidated manual gameplay pass per PR** for the visuals/audio that can't be verified headless (per `docs/testing.md`) — PR-A: companion look/collar/sit pose, tame hearts, bark/meow; PR-B: village layout, profession tints, raid pacing/audio.

**Delivery:**
- **PR-A** — once the gate is green, **push the branch and open the PR** against `hutusi/main` (user-authorized). No AI-attribution lines in the description.
- **PR-B** — branch off PR-A's merged `main`, build it locally, run the full gate, then **stop and hand it to the user for review before any push** ([[review-fixes-no-push]]). Do not push or open PR-B unprompted.

77	  const baseZ = player.position.z - mob.position.z;
78	  for (let spread = -1; spread <= 1; spread += 1) {
79	    scratchAim.set(baseX, baseY, baseZ);
80	    if (spread !== 0) scratchAim.applyAxisAngle(UP, spread * BOSS_SPREAD);
81	    spawnArrow(state, mob.position.x, eyeY, mob.position.z, scratchAim, {
82	      speed: BOSS_ARROW_SPEED,
83	      damage: BOSS_ARROW_DAMAGE * dmgScale,
84	      knockback: MOB_ARROW_KNOCKBACK,
85	      fromPlayer: false,
86	      ttl: ARROW_TTL
87	    });
88	  }
89	  emit({ type: "mobAttacked", kind: mob.kind });
90	}
91	
92	/**
93	 * The boss periodically conjures a skeleton or zombie nearby while it is engaged,
94	 * up to its own minion cap and the shared global hostile cap.
95	 */
96	function tickBossSummon(state: GameState, mob: MobState, dt: number, deps: MobTickDeps): void {
97	  mob.summonTimer = (mob.summonTimer ?? 0) - dt;
98	  if (mob.summonTimer > 0) return;
99	  mob.summonTimer = BOSS_SUMMON_INTERVAL_SECONDS;
100	
101	  let minions = 0;
102	  let hostiles = 0;
103	  for (const other of state.mobs) {
104	    if (!other.hostile) continue;
105	    hostiles += 1;
106	    if (other.kind !== "boss") minions += 1;
107	  }
108	  if (minions >= BOSS_MINION_CAP || hostiles >= HOSTILE_CAP) return;
109	
110	  const kind = deps.rng() < 0.5 ? "skeleton" : "zombie";
111	  const angle = deps.rng() * Math.PI * 2;
112	  const radius = 2 + deps.rng() * 2;
113	  const mx = mob.position.x + Math.cos(angle) * radius;
114	  const mz = mob.position.z + Math.sin(angle) * radius;
115	  const my = deps.surfaceYAt(mx, mz);
116	  pushMob(state, kind, true, mx, my, mz, deps.rng);
117	  deps.emit({ type: "mobSpawned", kind, x: mx, y: my, z: mz });
118	}
119	
120	export type MobTickDeps = {
121	  surfaceYAt: SurfaceYAtFn;
122	  applyDamage: (amount: number) => void;
123	  removeMobAt: (index: number) => void;
124	  rng: () => number;
125	  emit: EmitGameEvent;
126	};
127	
128	export function tickMobs(state: GameState, dt: number, deps: MobTickDeps): void {
129	  const { world, daylight, mobs, isDead } = state;
130	  const playerPosition = state.player.position;
131	  const playerVelocity = state.player.velocity;
132	  // Creative/Spectator players aren't a threat target — hostiles ignore them
133	  // entirely (no aggro, attacks, fuses, or summons), so they just wander.
134	  const threatened = mobsThreaten(state.gameMode);
135	  // Difficulty scales every hit a mob lands (melee + arrows): Easy 0.5×, Hard 1.5×.
136	  // Applied here at the strike, never by mutating the per-mob templates.
137	  const dmgScale = mobDamageMultiplier(state.difficulty);
138	
139	  for (let i = 0; i < mobs.length; i += 1) {
140	    const mob = mobs[i];
141	    // A mob killed earlier this tick (e.g. by an explosion) still awaits the
142	    // post-loop sweep — skip its AI so a corpse can't move or land a final hit.
143	    if (mob.hp <= 0) continue;
144	    mob.attackTimer -= dt;
145	    mob.turnTimer -= dt;
146	    const activeHostile = threatened && mob.hostile && (mob.kind !== "spider" || daylight < SPIDER_AGGRO_BELOW_DAYLIGHT);
147	
148	    scratchToPlayer.copy(playerPosition).sub(mob.position).setY(0);
149	    const distanceToPlayer = scratchToPlayer.length();
150	    scratchToPlayer3D.copy(playerPosition).sub(mob.position);
151	    const attackDistance = scratchToPlayer3D.length();
152	    const verticalGap = Math.abs(scratchToPlayer3D.y);
153	    let moveSpeed = mob.speed;
154	    const isBoss = mob.kind === "boss";
155	    const isRanged = MOB_TEMPLATES[mob.kind].ranged === true;
156	    let moveSign = 1;
157	
158	    if (activeHostile && distanceToPlayer < mob.detectRange) {
159	      if (distanceToPlayer > 0.001) mob.direction.lerp(scratchToPlayer.normalize(), 0.2).normalize();
160	      moveSpeed *= 1.15;
161	      // Skeletons kite (back off / hold in a standoff band); the boss bears down.
162	      if (isRanged && !isBoss) {
163	        if (distanceToPlayer < SKELETON_STANDOFF_MIN) moveSign = -1;
164	        else if (distanceToPlayer <= SKELETON_STANDOFF_MAX) moveSign = 0;
165	      }
166	    } else if (!mob.hostile && mob.kind !== "villager" && distanceToPlayer < 4.2) {
167	      // Animals flee when you get close; villagers don't, so you can walk up to trade.
168	      if (distanceToPlayer > 0.001) mob.direction.lerp(scratchToPlayer.normalize().multiplyScalar(-1), 0.2).normalize();
169	      moveSpeed *= 1.15;
170	    } else if (mob.turnTimer <= 0) {
171	      mob.direction.applyAxisAngle(UP, (deps.rng() - 0.5) * Math.PI).normalize();
172	      mob.turnTimer = 1.5 + deps.rng() * 4;
173	    }
174	    mob.moveSpeed = moveSpeed;
175	
176	    let nx = mob.position.x + mob.direction.x * moveSpeed * dt * moveSign;
177	    let nz = mob.position.z + mob.direction.z * moveSpeed * dt * moveSign;
178	
179	    if (nx < 2 || nz < 2 || nx > world.sizeX - 2 || nz > world.sizeZ - 2) {
180	      mob.direction.multiplyScalar(-1);
181	      nx = mob.position.x + mob.direction.x * moveSpeed * dt * moveSign;
182	      nz = mob.position.z + mob.direction.z * moveSpeed * dt * moveSign;
183	      mob.turnTimer = 1;
184	    }
185	
186	    let ground = deps.surfaceYAt(nx, nz);
187	    scratchMobFeet.set(nx, ground, nz);
188	    if (collidesAt(world, scratchMobFeet, 0.28, mob.halfHeight * 2)) {
189	      mob.direction.multiplyScalar(-1);
190	      nx = mob.position.x;
191	      nz = mob.position.z;
192	      ground = mob.position.y - mob.halfHeight;
193	      mob.turnTimer = 1;
194	    }
195	    mob.position.set(nx, ground + mob.halfHeight, nz);
196	    mob.yaw = Math.atan2(mob.direction.x, mob.direction.z);
197	
198	    // Ranged mobs shoot from across their detect range; melee mobs (and the boss
199	    // up close) must be adjacent. The boss reaches a little farther for melee.
200	    const meleeReach = isBoss ? BOSS_MELEE_REACH : 4;
201	    const meleeVGap = isBoss ? SKELETON_FIRE_VGAP : 1.6;
202	    const meleeReady = activeHostile && attackDistance < meleeReach && verticalGap < meleeVGap;
203	    const fireReady = isRanged && activeHostile && attackDistance < mob.detectRange && verticalGap < SKELETON_FIRE_VGAP;
204	    // A creeper close enough to light its fuse also needs a line-of-sight check —
205	    // it can be in range with a large vertical gap (so not meleeReady), which
206	    // would otherwise arm the fuse off the default `hasLineOfSight = true`.
207	    const creeperFuseReady = mob.kind === "creeper" && activeHostile && attackDistance < CREEPER_FUSE_RANGE;
208	
209	    let hasLineOfSight = true;
210	    if (meleeReady || fireReady || creeperFuseReady) {
211	      scratchMobEye.set(mob.position.x, mob.position.y + mob.halfHeight * 0.35, mob.position.z);
212	      scratchPlayerAim.set(playerPosition.x, playerPosition.y + 0.9, playerPosition.z);
213	      scratchRay.copy(scratchPlayerAim).sub(scratchMobEye);
214	      if (scratchRay.lengthSq() > 1e-6) {
215	        const hit = voxelRaycast(world, scratchMobEye, scratchRay.normalize(), attackDistance + 0.5);
216	        hasLineOfSight = hit === null;
217	      }
218	    }
219	
220	    // !isDead: mobs keep ticking through the respawn countdown, but attacking a
221	    // corpse should neither sound nor re-arm the attack cooldown.
222	    if (!isDead && (meleeReady || fireReady) && hasLineOfSight && mob.attackTimer <= 0) {
223	      // The boss bites when adjacent, otherwise looses a spread; skeletons only
224	      // ever shoot; melee mobs only ever bite. Creepers never bite — they detonate.
225	      const doMelee = meleeReady && (!isRanged || isBoss) && mob.kind !== "creeper";
226	      if (doMelee) {
227	        deps.emit({ type: "mobAttacked", kind: mob.kind });
228	        deps.applyDamage((isBoss ? BOSS_MELEE_DAMAGE : mob.attackDamage) * dmgScale);
229	        if (distanceToPlayer > 0.001) {
230	          scratchToPlayer.normalize().multiplyScalar(isBoss ? 6 : 4.2);
231	          playerVelocity.x += scratchToPlayer.x;
232	          playerVelocity.z += scratchToPlayer.z;
233	          playerVelocity.y = Math.max(playerVelocity.y, isBoss ? 4.5 : 3.4);
234	        }
235	      } else if (fireReady) {
236	        if (isBoss) fireBossSpread(state, mob, dmgScale, deps.emit);
237	        else fireMobArrow(state, mob, SKELETON_ARROW_DAMAGE * dmgScale, SKELETON_ARROW_SPEED, deps.emit);
238	      }
239	      mob.attackTimer = mob.attackCooldown;
240	    }
241	
242	    // The boss conjures minions while it is engaged with the player.
243	    if (!isDead && isBoss && activeHostile && distanceToPlayer < mob.detectRange) {
244	      tickBossSummon(state, mob, dt, deps);
245	    }
246	
247	    // A creeper lights its fuse when it gets close, then detonates — destroying
248	    // terrain and hurting the player and nearby mobs. Walk out of range while it
249	    // is primed and the fuse aborts. It dies in its own blast (dropping gunpowder
250	    // via the post-loop sweep); killing it before the fuse runs out cancels it.
251	    if (!isDead && mob.kind === "creeper") {
252	      if ((mob.fuseTimer ?? 0) > 0) {
253	        if (!activeHostile || distanceToPlayer > CREEPER_ABORT_RANGE) {
254	          mob.fuseTimer = 0;
255	        } else {
256	          mob.fuseTimer = (mob.fuseTimer ?? 0) - dt;
257	          if (mob.fuseTimer <= 0) {
258	            explode(state, mob.position.x, mob.position.y, mob.position.z, CREEPER_EXPLOSION_POWER, deps);
259	            mob.hp = 0;
260	          }
261	        }
262	      } else if (creeperFuseReady && hasLineOfSight) {
263	        mob.fuseTimer = CREEPER_FUSE_SECONDS;
264	        deps.emit({ type: "mobAttacked", kind: "creeper" }); // the hiss
265	      }
266	    }
267	
268	    // Zombies, skeletons, and creepers burn in broad daylight; the boss is immune.
269	    if (mob.hostile && mob.kind !== "spider" && mob.kind !== "boss" && daylight > HOSTILE_BURN_ABOVE_DAYLIGHT) {
270	      mob.hp -= dt * 0.8;
271	    }
272	  }
273	
274	  // Sweep the dead after the loop (descending, so splices don't shift live
275	  // indices). A post-loop sweep — not per-iteration — also catches mobs killed by
276	  // an explosion earlier in the same pass, including the creeper that just blew up.
277	  for (let i = mobs.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
278	    if (mobs[i].hp <= 0) deps.removeMobAt(i);
279	  }
280	}
281

124	/**
125	 * Body-center height above the ground for a mob kind. Mirrors the geometry
126	 * math in createMobModel so the headless simulation needs no Three.js meshes.
127	 */
128	export function mobHalfHeight(kind: MobKind): number {
129	  const bodyHeight = MOB_TEMPLATES[kind].modelArgs[5][1];
130	  const legHeight = Math.max(0.3, bodyHeight * 0.56);
131	  return Math.max(bodyHeight, legHeight) * 0.5 + 0.2;
132	}
133	
134	/** Builds the Three.js model for a mob kind (renderer side). */
135	export function createMobModelForKind(kind: MobKind) {
136	  return createMobModel(...MOB_TEMPLATES[kind].modelArgs);
137	}

20	export type SpawnGroupArgs = {
21	  kind: MobKind;
22	  hostile: boolean;
23	  count: number;
24	  centerX: number;

31	/** Adds one mob standing with its feet at (x, y, z) (y is the ground, not the body center). */
32	export function pushMob(state: GameState, kind: MobKind, hostile: boolean, x: number, y: number, z: number, rng: () => number): void {
33	  const template = MOB_TEMPLATES[kind];
34	  const halfHeight = mobHalfHeight(kind);
35	  const mob: MobState = {
36	    id: state.nextMobId,
37	    kind,
38	    hostile,
39	    hp: template.hp,
40	    position: new THREE.Vector3(x, y + halfHeight, z),
41	    direction: new THREE.Vector3(rng() - 0.5, 0, rng() - 0.5).normalize(),
42	    yaw: 0,
43	    turnTimer: 1 + rng() * 3,
44	    speed: template.speed,
45	    moveSpeed: template.speed,
46	    detectRange: template.detectRange,
47	    attackDamage: template.attackDamage,
48	    attackCooldown: template.attackCooldown,
49	    attackTimer: rng(),
50	    halfHeight,
51	    bobSeed: rng() * 10,
52	    fedTimer: 0,
53	    ageTimer: 0
54	  };
55	  state.nextMobId += 1;
56	  state.mobs.push(mob);
57	}
58	
59	/**
60	 * Spawns the single endgame boss with its feet at (x, y, z), bypassing the
61	 * hostile-cap directors (the totem summon is always allowed). Seeds its minion
62	 * timer so the first summon waits a full interval.
63	 */
64	export function spawnBoss(state: GameState, x: number, y: number, z: number, rng: () => number): void {
65	  pushMob(state, "boss", true, x, y, z, rng);
66	  state.mobs[state.mobs.length - 1].summonTimer = BOSS_SUMMON_INTERVAL_SECONDS;
67	}
68	
69	export function spawnMobGroup(state: GameState, args: SpawnGroupArgs, rng: () => number, surfaceYAt: SurfaceYAtFn): void {
70	  for (let i = 0; i < args.count; i += 1) {
71	    const spawnPos = randomLandPointNear(state.world, surfaceYAt, args.centerX, args.centerZ, args.radius, rng, args.minRadius ?? 0);
72	    pushMob(state, args.kind, args.hostile, spawnPos.x, spawnPos.y, spawnPos.z, rng);
73	  }
74	}
75	
76	/**
77	 * The day-one population around the player's spawn point. Passives scatter
78	 * over a wider ring than hostiles so the spawn area doesn't feel like a
79	 * petting zoo; hostiles stay closer (the dawn-aggro behavior tests document).
80	 */
81	export function spawnInitialMobs(state: GameState, rng: () => number, surfaceYAt: SurfaceYAtFn): void {
82	  const centerX = state.player.position.x;
83	  const centerZ = state.player.position.z;
84	  const passiveRadius = RENDER_RADIUS * 1.2;
85	  const hostileRadius = RENDER_RADIUS * 0.7;
86	  const groups: Array<[MobKind, boolean, number, number]> = [
87	    ["sheep", false, 6, passiveRadius],
88	    ["chicken", false, 5, passiveRadius],
89	    ["horse", false, 3, passiveRadius],
90	    ["cow", false, 4, passiveRadius],
91	    ["pig", false, 4, passiveRadius],
92	    ["villager", false, 3, passiveRadius],
93	    ["zombie", true, 8, hostileRadius],
94	    ["skeleton", true, 6, hostileRadius],
95	    ["spider", true, 6, hostileRadius],
96	    ["creeper", true, 4, hostileRadius]
97	  ];
98	  // Peaceful spawns no hostiles at all — only the passive groups populate the world.
99	  const spawnHostiles = hostilesSpawn(state.difficulty);
100	  for (const [kind, hostile, count, radius] of groups) {
101	    if (hostile && !spawnHostiles) continue;
102	    // Hostiles keep a minimum standoff so nothing (notably a creeper) starts the
103	    // game point-blank; passives may roam right up to the spawn area.
104	    spawnMobGroup(state, { kind, hostile, count, centerX, centerZ, radius, minRadius: hostile ? HOSTILE_SPAWN_MIN_RADIUS : 0 }, rng, surfaceYAt);
105	  }
106	}
107	
108	/** Trickles hostile mobs in around the player at night, up to the cap. Difficulty scales the cadence and cap; Peaceful spawns none. */
109	export function tickHostileSpawnDirector(state: GameState, dt: number, rng: () => number, surfaceYAt: SurfaceYAtFn): void {
110	  if (!hostilesSpawn(state.difficulty)) return;
111	  state.timers.hostileSpawnTimer += dt;
112	  const interval = HOSTILE_SPAWN_INTERVAL_SECONDS * hostileSpawnIntervalScale(state.difficulty);
113	  if (state.daylight >= HOSTILE_SPAWN_BELOW_DAYLIGHT || state.timers.hostileSpawnTimer < interval) return;
114	  state.timers.hostileSpawnTimer = 0;
115	
116	  const cap = Math.round(HOSTILE_CAP * hostileCapScale(state.difficulty));
117	  const livingHostiles = state.mobs.filter((mob) => mob.hostile).length;
118	  if (livingHostiles >= cap) return;
119	
120	  const spawnKinds: Array<"zombie" | "skeleton" | "spider" | "creeper"> = ["zombie", "skeleton", "spider", "creeper"];
121	  const kind = spawnKinds[Math.floor(rng() * spawnKinds.length)];
122	  // A wave is 1–2 mobs, but never more than the slots left under the cap — so a
123	  // 2-pack rolled at cap-1 can't overshoot (especially Easy's tighter cap of 8).
124	  spawnMobGroup(
125	    state,
126	    {
127	      kind,
128	      hostile: true,
129	      count: Math.min(cap - livingHostiles, 1 + (rng() > 0.7 ? 1 : 0)),
130	      centerX: state.player.position.x,
131	      centerZ: state.player.position.z,
132	      radius: Math.max(26, RENDER_RADIUS * 0.85),
133	      minRadius: HOSTILE_SPAWN_MIN_RADIUS
134	    },
135	    rng,
136	    surfaceYAt
137	  );
138	}
139	
140	const SPAWNER_KINDS: ReadonlyArray<"zombie" | "skeleton" | "spider"> = ["zombie", "skeleton", "spider"];
141	
142	/**
143	 * Drips hostiles from dungeon spawners. On each interval, every intact spawner
144	 * with the player inside its activation radius spawns one hostile on the room
145	 * floor (feet at the spawner's own y, not the surface), bounded by a local
146	 * cluster cap and the shared global HOSTILE_CAP. Time-independent — dungeons
147	 * are dark. Spawner positions come from the session-derived index set, so
148	 * mining out a spawner block stops it (the world.get check below).
149	 */
150	export function tickSpawnerDirector(state: GameState, dt: number, rng: () => number, emit: EmitGameEvent): void {
151	  if (!hostilesSpawn(state.difficulty)) return; // Peaceful keeps even dungeon spawners inert
152	  if (state.dungeonSpawnerIndices.size === 0) return;
153	  state.timers.spawnerTimer += dt;
154	  if (state.timers.spawnerTimer < SPAWNER_INTERVAL_SECONDS) return;
155	  state.timers.spawnerTimer = 0;
156	
157	  const cap = Math.round(HOSTILE_CAP * hostileCapScale(state.difficulty));
158	  const countHostiles = () => state.mobs.reduce((acc, mob) => acc + (mob.hostile ? 1 : 0), 0);
159	  if (countHostiles() >= cap) return;
160	
161	  const { player, world } = state;
162	  const layer = world.sizeX * world.sizeZ;
163	  for (const idx of state.dungeonSpawnerIndices) {
164	    const sy = Math.floor(idx / layer);
165	    const rem = idx - sy * layer;
166	    const sz = Math.floor(rem / world.sizeX);
167	    const sx = rem - sz * world.sizeX;
168	    if (world.get(sx, sy, sz) !== BlockId.Spawner) continue; // mined out → inert
169	    if (Math.hypot(player.position.x - (sx + 0.5), player.position.y - (sy + 0.5), player.position.z - (sz + 0.5)) > SPAWNER_ACTIVATION_RADIUS) continue;
170	    if (countHostiles() >= cap) break;
171	
172	    const nearby = state.mobs.reduce(
173	      (acc, mob) => acc + (mob.hostile && Math.hypot(mob.position.x - (sx + 0.5), mob.position.z - (sz + 0.5)) <= SPAWNER_ACTIVATION_RADIUS ? 1 : 0),
174	      0
175	    );
176	    if (nearby >= SPAWNER_LOCAL_CAP) continue;
177	
178	    const kind = SPAWNER_KINDS[Math.floor(rng() * SPAWNER_KINDS.length)];
179	    const jx = sx + 0.5 + (rng() * 2 - 1) * 1.2;
180	    const jz = sz + 0.5 + (rng() * 2 - 1) * 1.2;
181	    pushMob(state, kind, true, jx, sy, jz, rng);
182	    emit({ type: "mobSpawned", kind, x: sx + 0.5, y: sy + 0.5, z: sz + 0.5 });
183	  }
184	}

7	/**
8	 * Animal breeding. Each tick ages babies up and counts down the "in love"
9	 * window; on an interval it pairs two fed adults of the same kind that are close
10	 * together into a baby, bounded by PASSIVE_CAP. Mobs are never persisted, so
11	 * breeding state is session-only by the engine's existing design.
12	 */
13	export function tickBreeding(state: GameState, dt: number, rng: () => number, surfaceYAt: SurfaceYAtFn, emit: EmitGameEvent): void {
14	  const { mobs } = state;
15	
16	  // Per-tick: tick down love + maturity timers; a matured baby regains full size.
17	  for (const mob of mobs) {
18	    if (mob.fedTimer > 0) mob.fedTimer = Math.max(0, mob.fedTimer - dt);
19	    if (mob.ageTimer > 0) {
20	      mob.ageTimer = Math.max(0, mob.ageTimer - dt);
21	      if (mob.ageTimer === 0) mob.halfHeight = mobHalfHeight(mob.kind);
22	    }
23	  }
24	
25	  state.timers.breedTimer += dt;
26	  if (state.timers.breedTimer < BREED_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS) return;
27	  state.timers.breedTimer = 0;
28	
29	  let passiveCount = mobs.reduce((acc, mob) => acc + (mob.hostile ? 0 : 1), 0);
30	  const radiusSq = BREED_PARTNER_RADIUS * BREED_PARTNER_RADIUS;
31	
32	  for (let i = 0; i < mobs.length; i += 1) {
33	    if (passiveCount >= PASSIVE_CAP) break;
34	    const a = mobs[i];
35	    if (a.hostile || a.fedTimer <= 0 || a.ageTimer > 0) continue;
36	    for (let j = i + 1; j < mobs.length; j += 1) {
37	      const b = mobs[j];
38	      if (b.hostile || b.kind !== a.kind || b.fedTimer <= 0 || b.ageTimer > 0) continue;
39	      if (a.position.distanceToSquared(b.position) > radiusSq) continue;
40	
41	      spawnBaby(state, a, rng, surfaceYAt);
42	      passiveCount += 1;
43	      a.fedTimer = 0;
44	      b.fedTimer = 0;
45	      emit({ type: "mobBred", kind: a.kind });
46	      break; // a has bred; move to the next animal
47	    }
48	  }
49	}
50	
51	/** Spawns a juvenile of the parent's kind at the midpoint, scaled down until grown. */
52	function spawnBaby(state: GameState, parent: MobState, rng: () => number, surfaceYAt: SurfaceYAtFn): void {
53	  const template = MOB_TEMPLATES[parent.kind];
54	  const halfHeight = mobHalfHeight(parent.kind) * BABY_SCALE;
55	  const x = parent.position.x;
56	  const z = parent.position.z;
57	  const baby: MobState = {
58	    id: state.nextMobId,
59	    kind: parent.kind,
60	    hostile: false,
61	    hp: template.hp,
62	    position: new THREE.Vector3(x, surfaceYAt(x, z) + halfHeight, z),
63	    direction: new THREE.Vector3(rng() - 0.5, 0, rng() - 0.5).normalize(),
64	    yaw: 0,
65	    turnTimer: 1 + rng() * 3,
66	    speed: template.speed,
67	    moveSpeed: template.speed,
68	    detectRange: template.detectRange,
69	    attackDamage: template.attackDamage,
70	    attackCooldown: template.attackCooldown,
71	    attackTimer: rng(),
72	    halfHeight,
73	    bobSeed: rng() * 10,
74	    fedTimer: 0,
75	    ageTimer: BABY_GROW_SECONDS
76	  };
77	  state.nextMobId += 1;
78	  state.mobs.push(baby);
79	}

37	/** Coerces a persisted hotbar index to a finite integer within 0..HOTBAR_SLOTS-1. */
38	function normalizeSelectedSlot(value: number): number {
39	  const index = Number.isFinite(value) ? Math.floor(value) : 0;
40	  return Math.max(0, Math.min(HOTBAR_SLOTS - 1, index));

43	export function migrateSaveV1toV2(save: SaveDataV1): SaveDataV2 {
44	  const migrated: SaveDataV2 = { ...save, version: 2, selectedSlot: normalizeSelectedSlot(save.selectedSlot) };
45	
46	  if (Array.isArray(save.inventorySlots)) {
47	    const packed: Array<{ id: string | null; count: number; durability?: number }> = [];
48	    for (const saved of save.inventorySlots) {
49	      if (!saved?.id || saved.count <= 0) continue;
50	      // Items without durability stack; merge them into an earlier stack first.
51	      const stackable = ITEM_DEF_BY_ID[saved.id] ? !ITEM_DEF_BY_ID[saved.id].maxDurability : false;
52	      let remaining = saved.count;
53	      if (stackable) {
54	        for (const slot of packed) {
55	          if (slot.id !== saved.id || slot.count >= MAX_STACK_SIZE) continue;
56	          const moved = Math.min(MAX_STACK_SIZE - slot.count, remaining);
57	          slot.count += moved;
58	          remaining -= moved;
59	          if (remaining === 0) break;
60	        }
61	      }
62	      while (remaining > 0 && packed.length < INVENTORY_SLOTS) {
63	        const moved = Math.min(maxStackSizeForItem(saved.id), remaining);
64	        packed.push({ id: saved.id, count: moved, durability: saved.durability });
65	        remaining -= moved;
66	      }
67	    }
68	    migrated.inventorySlots = packed;
69	  }
70	
71	  return migrated;
72	}

281	/** Validates persisted enchantments: known ids and integer levels clamped to 1..(that enchant's max); undefined when none survive. */
282	function restoreEnchantments(saved: SavedSlot["enchantments"]): Enchantment[] | undefined {
283	  if (!Array.isArray(saved)) return undefined;
284	  const out: Enchantment[] = [];
285	  for (const entry of saved) {
286	    if (!entry || typeof entry.id !== "string" || !Object.hasOwn(VALID_ENCHANT_IDS, entry.id)) continue;
287	    if (!Number.isFinite(entry.level) || Math.floor(entry.level) < 1) continue;
288	    // Clamp to the enchantment's own cap so e.g. a tampered mending:3 loads as 1.

294	/**
295	 * Rebuilds one slot from its saved snapshot: drops unknown ids, clamps the
296	 * count, and clamps/defaults durability for gear (a non-positive saved
297	 * durability means the piece broke and is dropped). Returns an empty slot for
298	 * anything invalid. Shared by inventory and container restore.
299	 */
300	function restoreSlot(saved: SavedSlot | undefined): InventorySlot {
301	  if (!saved?.id || saved.count <= 0 || !ITEM_DEF_BY_ID[saved.id]) return createEmptySlot();
302	  const slot = createSlot(saved.id, Math.min(maxStackSizeForItem(saved.id), Math.max(0, Math.floor(saved.count))));
303	  if ((slot.kind === "tool" || slot.kind === "weapon" || slot.kind === "armor") && slot.maxDurability) {
304	    if (typeof saved.durability === "number") {
305	      const loaded = Math.floor(saved.durability);
306	      if (loaded <= 0) return createEmptySlot();
307	      slot.durability = Math.max(1, Math.min(slot.maxDurability, loaded));
308	    } else {
309	      slot.durability = slot.maxDurability;
310	    }
311	    // Enchantments live only on durable gear; validated against the known set.
312	    const enchantments = restoreEnchantments(saved.enchantments);
313	    if (enchantments) slot.enchantments = enchantments;
314	    // A custom name (anvil rename) also lives only on durable gear; trim and cap it.
315	    if (typeof saved.customName === "string") {
316	      const name = saved.customName.trim().slice(0, CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN);
317	      if (name) slot.customName = name;
318	    }
319	  }
320	  return slot;

447	    const slots = Array.from({ length: INVENTORY_SLOTS }, () => createEmptySlot());

449	    for (const [id, raw] of Object.entries(save.inventoryCounts)) {
450	      if (!ITEM_DEF_BY_ID[id]) continue;
451	      let remaining = Math.max(0, Math.floor(raw));
452	      while (remaining > 0 && cursor < slots.length) {
453	        const add = Math.min(maxStackSizeForItem(id), remaining);
454	        slots[cursor] = createSlot(id, add);
455	        cursor += 1;
456	        remaining -= add;
457	      }
458	    }
459	    return slots;
460	  }
461	
462	  return null;
463	}

465	/** Restores worn armor, rebuilding each piece through restoreSlot and dropping anything that isn't valid armor for its slot. */
466	export function restoreEquippedArmor(save: SaveData): EquippedArmor | null {
467	  if (!save.equippedArmor) return null;
468	  const next = createEmptyArmorEquipment();
469	  for (const armorSlot of ARMOR_SLOTS) {
470	    const saved = save.equippedArmor[armorSlot];
471	    if (!saved) continue;
472	    const slot = restoreSlot(saved);
473	    if (slot.kind !== "armor" || slot.armorSlot !== armorSlot || slot.count <= 0) continue;
474	    next[armorSlot] = slot;
475	  }
476	  return next;
477	}

492	  if (typeof save.hearts !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(save.hearts)) return null;
493	  return Math.max(1, Math.min(MAX_HEARTS, Math.floor(save.hearts)));

224	export function tryUseHeldItem(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent, rng: () => number): boolean {
225	  const slot = state.inventory[state.selectedSlot];
226	  if (!slot?.id || slot.count <= 0) return false;
227	  const isHoe = slot.id.endsWith("_hoe");
228	  const isSeeds = slot.id === "seeds";
229	  const isTorch = slot.id === "torch";
230	  const isSapling = slot.id === "sapling";
231	  const isBoneMeal = slot.id === "bone_meal";
232	  if (!isHoe && !isSeeds && !isTorch && !isSapling && !isBoneMeal) return false;
233	
234	  const { world, player } = state;
235	  scratchEye.set(player.position.x, player.position.y + EYE_HEIGHT, player.position.z);
236	  lookDirection(player.yaw, player.pitch, scratchDir);
237	  const result = voxelRaycast(world, scratchEye, scratchDir, MINE_REACH);
238	  if (!result) return false;
239	  const { x, y, z } = result.hit;
240	  const block = world.get(x, y, z) as BlockId;
241	
242	  // Light TNT with a torch (the torch is not consumed). Only consumes the click
243	  // when actually aimed at TNT, so a torch otherwise still places normally.
244	  if (isTorch) {
245	    if (block !== BlockId.Tnt) return false;
246	    primeTnt(state, x, y, z, emit);
247	    return true;
248	  }
249	
250	  // Bone meal: fertilize. Instantly grows an aimed sapling into a tree, or
251	  // advances an immature crop a random 1..MAX stages. Consumes one per use.
252	  if (isBoneMeal) {
253	    if (block === BlockId.Sapling) {
254	      growTreeAt(state, x, y, z, rng);
255	    } else if (block >= BlockId.WheatStage0 && block <= BlockId.WheatStage2) {
256	      const next = Math.min(block + 1 + Math.floor(rng() * BONE_MEAL_CROP_STAGES_MAX), BlockId.WheatStage3) as BlockId;
257	      state.blockChanges.set(x, y, z, next);
258	      state.worldMeshDirty = true;
259	    } else {
260	      return false;
261	    }
262	    state.inventory = adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, slot.id, -1, state.selectedSlot) ?? state.inventory;
263	    emit({ type: "usedBoneMeal" });
264	    return true;
265	  }
266	
267	  if (isHoe) {
268	    if (block !== BlockId.Grass && block !== BlockId.Dirt) return false;
269	    state.blockChanges.set(x, y, z, BlockId.Farmland);
270	    state.inventory = consumeToolDurability(state.inventory, state.selectedSlot, 1, rng) ?? state.inventory;
271	    state.worldMeshDirty = true;
272	    emit({ type: "tilledSoil" });

101	/** True when the held slot is a usable bow (the attack input fires instead of melees). */
102	export function isBow(slot: InventorySlot | undefined): boolean {
103	  return slot?.id === "bow" && slot.count > 0;
104	}

106	/**
107	 * Fires one arrow from the player's eye along their look direction, consuming an
108	 * arrow and a point of bow durability and arming the fire-rate cooldown. Returns
109	 * false (no shot) when the bow is on cooldown or the player has no arrows — the
110	 * caller has already confirmed a bow is held via isBow, so a bow never melees.
111	 */
112	export function tryFireBow(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent, rng?: () => number): boolean {
113	  const slot = state.inventory[state.selectedSlot];
114	  if (!isBow(slot)) return false;
115	  if (state.timers.bowCooldownTimer > 0) return false;
116	  if ((countsById(state.inventory).get("arrow") ?? 0) < 1) return false;
117	
118	  const { position, yaw, pitch } = state.player;
119	  scratchOrigin.set(position.x, position.y + EYE_HEIGHT, position.z);
120	  lookDirection(yaw, pitch, scratchForward);
121	  // Power and Punch are bow-only enchants, read off the held bow at the one fire seam.
122	  spawnArrow(state, scratchOrigin.x, scratchOrigin.y, scratchOrigin.z, scratchForward, {
123	    speed: ARROW_SPEED,
124	    damage: BOW_ARROW_DAMAGE + powerBonus(slot),
125	    knockback: BOW_KNOCKBACK + punchKnockback(slot),
126	    fromPlayer: true,
127	    ttl: ARROW_TTL
128	  });
129	
130	  state.inventory = adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, "arrow", -1) ?? state.inventory;
131	  state.inventory = consumeToolDurability(state.inventory, state.selectedSlot, BOW_DURABILITY_PER_SHOT, rng) ?? state.inventory;
132	  state.timers.bowCooldownTimer = BOW_COOLDOWN_SECONDS;
133	  emit({ type: "bowFired" });
134	  return true;
135	}

18	  return block === BlockId.Bedrock || block === BlockId.Spawner || block === BlockId.Lava;

23	  switch (block) {
24	    case BlockId.Stone:
25	    case BlockId.Cobblestone:
26	    case BlockId.Brick:
27	    case BlockId.MossyCobblestone:
28	    case BlockId.Furnace:

30	    case BlockId.SliverOre:
31	    case BlockId.RubyOre:
32	    case BlockId.GoldOre:
33	    case BlockId.SapphireOre:
34	    case BlockId.DiamondOre:
35	      return 2.5;
36	    case BlockId.Chest:
37	      return 1.2;

39	      return 0.4; // dirt, sand, wood, planks, leaves, glass, doors, crops, torches, ...

  "new_string": "const scratchMobFeet = new THREE.Vector3();\nconst scratchAim = new THREE.Vector3();\nconst scratchToTarget = new THREE.Vector3();\n\nconst NO_ENEMIES: ReadonlySet<MobFaction> = new Set<MobFaction>();\n\n/**\n * The shared enmity table — which factions each faction will attack. \"Fighters\"\n * (hostile/raider/ally) hunt enemy-faction mobs; wild animals and villagers never\n * fight. Hostiles & raiders go after villagers and pets; pets defend against\n * hostiles & raiders.\n */\nconst ENEMY_FACTIONS: Record<MobFaction, ReadonlySet<MobFaction>> = {\n  wild: NO_ENEMIES,\n  villager: NO_ENEMIES,\n  hostile: new Set<MobFaction>([\"villager\", \"ally\"]),\n  raider: new Set<MobFaction>([\"villager\", \"ally\"]),\n  ally: new Set<MobFaction>([\"hostile\", \"raider\"])\n};\n\n/** Factions a villager flees from. */\nconst THREAT_FACTIONS: ReadonlySet<MobFaction> = new Set<MobFaction>([\"hostile\", \"raider\"]);\n\n/**\n * Victim factions whose death credits the player with loot + XP. A pet's kill\n * still feeds you (\"your wolf hunts for you\"); a slain villager or pet yields\n * nothing — which also closes the XP leak of farming mobs that kill each other.\n */\nconst CREDITED_FACTIONS: ReadonlySet<MobFaction> = new Set<MobFaction>([\"wild\", \"hostile\", \"raider\"]);\n\nfunction horizDistSq(a: MobState, b: MobState): number {\n  const dx = a.position.x - b.position.x;\n  const dz = a.position.z - b.position.z;\n  return dx * dx + dz * dz;\n}\n\nfunction mobById(state: GameState, id: number): MobState | null {\n  for (const other of state.mobs) if (other.id === id) return other;\n  return null;\n}\n\n/**\n * The mob (if any) this fighter is hunting. It keeps its cached `targetId` while\n * that mob is alive, still an enemy, and in range; otherwise it re-scans for the\n * nearest enemy-faction mob — but only every MOB_RETARGET_SECONDS, so the per-mob\n * tick stays O(N) and full scans amortize to ~1–2 Hz per fighter. Non-fighters\n * (wild/villager) have no enemies and return null immediately.\n */\nfunction selectMobTarget(state: GameState, mob: MobState): MobState | null {\n  const enemies = ENEMY_FACTIONS[mob.faction];\n  if (enemies.size === 0) return null;\n  const rangeSq = mob.detectRange * mob.detectRange;\n  if (mob.targetId !== null && mob.retargetTimer > 0) {\n    const cached = mobById(state, mob.targetId);\n    if (cached && cached.hp > 0 && enemies.has(cached.faction) && horizDistSq(mob, cached) < rangeSq) return cached;\n  }\n  mob.retargetTimer = MOB_RETARGET_SECONDS;\n  let best: MobState | null = null;\n  let bestSq = rangeSq;\n  for (const other of state.mobs) {\n    if (other === mob || other.hp <= 0 || !enemies.has(other.faction)) continue;\n    const d = horizDistSq(mob, other);\n    if (d < bestSq) {\n      bestSq = d;\n      best = other;\n    }\n  }\n  mob.targetId = best ? best.id : null;\n  return best;\n}\n\n/** Nearest hostile/raider within `range` of a villager (drives its flee), or null. */\nfunction nearestThreat(state: GameState, mob: MobState, range: number): MobState | null {\n  let best: MobState | null = null;\n  let bestSq = range * range;\n  for (const other of state.mobs) {\n    if (other.hp <= 0 || !THREAT_FACTIONS.has(other.faction)) continue;\n    const d = horizDistSq(mob, other);\n    if (d < bestSq) {\n      bestSq = d;\n      best = other;\n    }\n  }\n  return best;\n}"
}

218	  const { world, daylight, mobs, isDead } = state;
219	  const playerPosition = state.player.position;

225	  // Applied here at the strike, never by mutating the per-mob templates.
226	  const dmgScale = mobDamageMultiplier(state.difficulty);
227	
228	  for (let i = 0; i < mobs.length; i += 1) {
229	    const mob = mobs[i];
230	    // A mob killed earlier this tick (e.g. by an explosion) still awaits the
231	    // post-loop sweep — skip its AI so a corpse can't move or land a final hit.
232	    if (mob.hp <= 0) continue;
233	    mob.attackTimer -= dt;
234	    mob.turnTimer -= dt;
235	    const activeHostile = threatened && mob.hostile && (mob.kind !== "spider" || daylight < SPIDER_AGGRO_BELOW_DAYLIGHT);
236	
237	    scratchToPlayer.copy(playerPosition).sub(mob.position).setY(0);
238	    const distanceToPlayer = scratchToPlayer.length();
239	    scratchToPlayer3D.copy(playerPosition).sub(mob.position);
240	    const attackDistance = scratchToPlayer3D.length();
241	    const verticalGap = Math.abs(scratchToPlayer3D.y);
242	    let moveSpeed = mob.speed;
243	    const isBoss = mob.kind === "boss";
244	    const isRanged = MOB_TEMPLATES[mob.kind].ranged === true;
245	    let moveSign = 1;
246	
247	    if (activeHostile && distanceToPlayer < mob.detectRange) {
248	      if (distanceToPlayer > 0.001) mob.direction.lerp(scratchToPlayer.normalize(), 0.2).normalize();
249	      moveSpeed *= 1.15;
250	      // Skeletons kite (back off / hold in a standoff band); the boss bears down.
251	      if (isRanged && !isBoss) {
252	        if (distanceToPlayer < SKELETON_STANDOFF_MIN) moveSign = -1;
253	        else if (distanceToPlayer <= SKELETON_STANDOFF_MAX) moveSign = 0;
254	      }
255	    } else if (!mob.hostile && mob.kind !== "villager" && distanceToPlayer < 4.2) {
256	      // Animals flee when you get close; villagers don't, so you can walk up to trade.
257	      if (distanceToPlayer > 0.001) mob.direction.lerp(scratchToPlayer.normalize().multiplyScalar(-1), 0.2).normalize();
258	      moveSpeed *= 1.15;

260	      mob.direction.applyAxisAngle(UP, (deps.rng() - 0.5) * Math.PI).normalize();
261	      mob.turnTimer = 1.5 + deps.rng() * 4;
262	    }

271	      nz = mob.position.z + mob.direction.z * moveSpeed * dt * moveSign;
272	      mob.turnTimer = 1;
273	    }

  "old_string": "  private removeMobAt = (index: number, lootingLevel = 0): void => {\n    const state = this.state;\n    const mob = state.mobs[index];\n    state.mobs.splice(index, 1);\n    // Babies drop nothing — only grown animals yield loot. `lootingLevel` is the\n    // *killing* melee weapon's Looting (forwarded by tryAttackMob); indirect kills\n    // (arrows, thrown spears, explosions) pass 0, since Looting is a melee enchant.\n    const drops = mob.ageTimer <= 0 ? rollMobDrops(mob.kind, this.rng, lootingLevel) : [];\n    for (const drop of drops) {\n      state.inventory = inv.adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, drop.itemId, drop.count) ?? state.inventory;\n    }\n    // XP on kill, baby-gated like drops; the boss pays a jackpot.\n    if (mob.ageTimer <= 0) awardXp(state, xpForMob(mob.kind), this.emit);\n    this.emit({ type: \"mobDied\", kind: mob.kind, x: mob.position.x, y: mob.position.y, z: mob.position.z });\n    // Drops land straight in inventory (no ground item), so announce them.\n    if (drops.length > 0) this.emit({ type: \"pickedUp\", items: drops });",
  "new_string": "  // `credit` (default true) gates loot + XP to the player: player/arrow/spear/\n  // explosion kills credit; the mobAI sweep passes the victim's faction so a pet's\n  // kill still feeds you, but a slain villager or pet yields nothing.\n  private removeMobAt = (index: number, lootingLevel = 0, credit = true): void => {\n    const state = this.state;\n    const mob = state.mobs[index];\n    state.mobs.splice(index, 1);\n    // Babies drop nothing — only grown animals yield loot. `lootingLevel` is the\n    // *killing* melee weapon's Looting (forwarded by tryAttackMob); indirect kills\n    // (arrows, thrown spears, explosions) pass 0, since Looting is a melee enchant.\n    const drops = credit && mob.ageTimer <= 0 ? rollMobDrops(mob.kind, this.rng, lootingLevel) : [];\n    for (const drop of drops) {\n      state.inventory = inv.adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, drop.itemId, drop.count) ?? state.inventory;\n    }\n    // XP on kill, baby-gated like drops; the boss pays a jackpot.\n    if (credit && mob.ageTimer <= 0) awardXp(state, xpForMob(mob.kind), this.emit);\n    this.emit({ type: \"mobDied\", kind: mob.kind, x: mob.position.x, y: mob.position.y, z: mob.position.z });\n    // Drops land straight in inventory (no ground item), so announce them.\n    if (drops.length > 0) this.emit({ type: \"pickedUp\", items: drops });"

  "command": "git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'\nfeat(mobs): allegiance + mob-vs-mob combat\n\nMob AI was strictly binary — passives flee the player, hostiles attack the\nplayer, and nothing ever fights anything else. That makes the world feel\ninert and blocks the upcoming companion/raid work, where pets must fight\nhostiles and raiders must attack villagers.\n\nAdd a `faction` axis (wild/hostile/ally/villager/raider) to MobState,\ncoexisting with the load-bearing `hostile` flag (which still gates caps,\nthe health bar, and Peaceful despawn). `faction` drives a shared enmity\ntable and `selectMobTarget`: a \"fighter\" (hostile/ally/raider) locks onto\nthe nearest enemy-faction mob within detect range, re-scanning only every\nMOB_RETARGET_SECONDS so steering stays O(N). Player aggro keeps strict\npriority, so every existing dawn-aggro behaviour is unchanged. Villagers\nnow flee the nearest hostile/raider; wild animals still flee the player.\n\nMob-vs-mob strikes are melee-only (the arrow hit-filter is a binary\nfromPlayer flag) and use the mob's raw attackDamage — difficulty scaling\napplies to player-facing damage only. removeMobAt gains a `credit` flag\n(default true, so every existing call site is unchanged); the death sweep\ncredits loot + XP by the victim's faction, so a pet's kill still feeds you\nbut a slain villager/pet yields nothing (also closing the XP leak of mobs\nfarming each other).\n\nNo save or worldgen change — the new fields are session-only for now\n(persisted in the following commit).\nEOF\ngit log --oneline -1",
  "description": "Commit c1"
}

> AGENT

I discovered an important nuance: villagers (faction "villager") are still loose-spawned by `spawnInitialMobs` every boot, so persisting them in PR-A would *double* them each reload. So in PR-A, `isPersistentMob` must be **pets only** (`owner != null`); village residents join the persistent set in PR-B when villages replace the loose villager spawns. Let me update the SavedMob doc to reflect that, then implement.

  "new_string": "/** Reads the unlocked advancement ids from a save (non-empty strings only, de-duplicated). */\nexport function restoreAdvancements(save: SaveData): string[] {\n  if (!Array.isArray(save.advancements)) return [];\n  const seen = new Set<string>();\n  for (const id of save.advancements) {\n    if (typeof id === \"string\" && id) seen.add(id);\n  }\n  return [...seen];\n}\n\n// Every known faction, keyed so a new MobFaction is a compile error here.\nconst VALID_MOB_FACTIONS: Record<MobFaction, true> = { wild: true, hostile: true, ally: true, villager: true, raider: true };\n\n/**\n * Whether a mob survives a save/reload. PR-A persists only tamed pets; the\n * fungible wild/hostile population (and the loose villagers) is re-seeded each\n * boot by spawnInitialMobs, so persisting it would just duplicate it. PR-B\n * widens this to include village residents.\n */\nexport function isPersistentMob(mob: MobState): boolean {\n  return mob.owner != null;\n}\n\n/** Snapshots the persistent mobs (tamed pets) for the save — body-center position + the state a template can't rebuild. */\nexport function serializeMobs(mobs: MobState[]): SavedMob[] {\n  const out: SavedMob[] = [];\n  for (const mob of mobs) {\n    if (!isPersistentMob(mob)) continue;\n    const saved: SavedMob = { kind: mob.kind, x: mob.position.x, y: mob.position.y, z: mob.position.z, hp: mob.hp, faction: mob.faction };\n    if (mob.owner != null) saved.owner = mob.owner;\n    if (mob.sitting) saved.sitting = true;\n    if (mob.ageTimer > 0) saved.ageTimer = mob.ageTimer;\n    out.push(saved);\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\n/**\n * Reads persisted mobs from a save into validated SavedMob entries — dropping\n * unknown kinds, non-finite coords, non-positive/garbage hp, and unknown factions.\n * The engine rebuilds the live MobState from these (re-grounding y onto current\n * terrain, assigning fresh ids), so this stays pure data — no THREE / no rng.\n */\nexport function restoreMobs(save: SaveData): SavedMob[] {\n  if (!Array.isArray(save.mobs)) return [];\n  const out: SavedMob[] = [];\n  for (const entry of save.mobs) {\n    if (!entry || typeof entry.kind !== \"string\" || !MOB_TEMPLATES[entry.kind]) continue;\n    if (!Number.isFinite(entry.x) || !Number.isFinite(entry.y) || !Number.isFinite(entry.z)) continue;\n    if (!Number.isFinite(entry.hp) || entry.hp <= 0) continue;\n    if (typeof entry.faction !== \"string\" || !Object.hasOwn(VALID_MOB_FACTIONS, entry.faction)) continue;\n    const saved: SavedMob = { kind: entry.kind, x: entry.x, y: entry.y, z: entry.z, hp: entry.hp, faction: entry.faction };\n    if (entry.owner === \"player\") saved.owner = \"player\";\n    if (entry.sitting === true) saved.sitting = true;\n    if (Number.isFinite(entry.ageTimer) && (entry.ageTimer ?? 0) > 0) saved.ageTimer = entry.ageTimer;\n    out.push(saved);\n  }\n  return out;\n}"
}

5	 * A single loot entry: yields a uniformly random count in [min, max], gated by

9	  itemId: string;

11	  max: number;

21	export const MOB_DROPS: Record<MobKind, MobDrop[]> = {
22	  sheep: [
23	    { itemId: "wool", min: 1, max: 2 },
24	    { itemId: "raw_mutton", min: 1, max: 1 }

29	  ],

34	  ],

36	  zombie: [{ itemId: "rotten_flesh", min: 1, max: 2 }],
37	  skeleton: [{ itemId: "bone", min: 1, max: 2 }],
38	  spider: [{ itemId: "string", min: 0, max: 2 }],
39	  creeper: [{ itemId: "gunpowder", min: 1, max: 2 }],
40	  // Villagers are non-combat trade NPCs — killing one yields nothing (don't murder
41	  // your shopkeeper). The empty table is intentional; mobLoot.test.ts allows it.
42	  villager: [],
43	  boss: [
44	    { itemId: "dragon_heart", min: 1, max: 1 },
45	    { itemId: "diamond_ore", min: 2, max: 4 }
46	  ]
47	};

49	/** Clamps an rng sample into [0, 1) so a pathological injected rng can't over-roll. */
50	const clampUnit = (v: number): number => Math.min(1 - Number.EPSILON, Math.max(0, v));
51	
52	/**
53	 * Rolls the drop table for a mob kind. Returns one entry per item that yielded a
54	 * positive count; the engine adds each to the inventory. `rng` is injectable so
55	 * tests get deterministic counts (0 → min, ~1 → max). `lootingLevel` (from the
56	 * Looting enchantment on the killing weapon) adds a random bonus count — up to
57	 * `level × LOOTING_BONUS_PER_LEVEL` extra — to each entry that already dropped.
58	 */
59	export function rollMobDrops(kind: MobKind, rng: () => number, lootingLevel = 0): Array<{ itemId: string; count: number }> {
60	  const drops: Array<{ itemId: string; count: number }> = [];
61	  for (const entry of MOB_DROPS[kind]) {
62	    if (entry.chance !== undefined && clampUnit(rng()) >= entry.chance) continue;
63	    const span = entry.max - entry.min + 1;
64	    let count = entry.min + Math.floor(clampUnit(rng()) * span);
65	    if (count > 0 && lootingLevel > 0) {
66	      count += Math.floor(clampUnit(rng()) * (lootingLevel * LOOTING_BONUS_PER_LEVEL + 1));
67	    }
68	    if (count > 0) drops.push({ itemId: entry.itemId, count });
69	  }
70	  return drops;
71	}

45	  const nextInterval = (kind: MobKind): number => {
46	    const [min, max] = CALL_INTERVALS[kind];
47	    return min + rng() * (max - min);
48	  };
49	
50	  return {
51	    tick(dt, mobs, playerX, playerZ, playerYaw) {
52	      calls.length = 0;
53	
54	      // Despawned mobs leave stale timers behind; sweep once the map outgrows
55	      // the population instead of allocating an id set every frame.
56	      if (timers.size > mobs.length + 8) {
57	        const alive = new Set(mobs.map((mob) => mob.id));
58	        for (const id of timers.keys()) if (!alive.has(id)) timers.delete(id);
59	      }
60	
61	      const rightX = Math.cos(playerYaw);
62	      const rightZ = -Math.sin(playerYaw);
63	
64	      for (const mob of mobs) {
65	        const dx = mob.position.x - playerX;
66	        const dz = mob.position.z - playerZ;
67	        const dist = Math.hypot(dx, dz);
68	        if (dist > MOB_EARSHOT) continue;
69	
70	        const timer = timers.get(mob.id);
71	        if (timer === undefined) {
72	          // First sighting: start a full randomized interval so a spawn wave
73	          // doesn't open with a chorus.
74	          timers.set(mob.id, nextInterval(mob.kind));
75	          continue;
76	        }
77	        const remaining = timer - dt;
78	        if (remaining > 0) {
79	          timers.set(mob.id, remaining);
80	          continue;
81	        }
82	        timers.set(mob.id, nextInterval(mob.kind));
83	
84	        const falloff = 1 - dist / MOB_EARSHOT;
85	        const pan = dist > 0.001 ? Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, (dx * rightX + dz * rightZ) / dist)) : 0;
86	        calls.push({ kind: mob.kind, gain: falloff * falloff, pan });
87	      }
88	      return calls;
89	    }
90	  };
91	}
92

1	import * as THREE from "three";
2	import { BABY_SCALE } from "@/lib/game/config";
3	import { createMobModelForKind, MOB_TEMPLATES } from "@/lib/game/mobs";
4	import type { MobModel } from "@/lib/game/types";
5	import type { MobState } from "@/lib/game/engine/state";
6	
7	type HealthBar = {
8	  group: THREE.Group;
9	  fill: THREE.Sprite;
10	  materials: THREE.SpriteMaterial[];
11	  width: number;
12	};
13	
14	type MobVisual = {
15	  model: MobModel;
16	  healthBar: HealthBar | null;
17	};
18	
19	export type MobVisuals = {
20	  /** Creates/removes models to match the mob list and animates bob + gait. */
21	  sync(mobs: MobState[], timeMs: number): void;
22	  dispose(): void;
23	};
24	
25	function createHealthBar(kind: MobState["kind"]): HealthBar {
26	  const [bodySize, headSize] = [MOB_TEMPLATES[kind].modelArgs[5], MOB_TEMPLATES[kind].modelArgs[6]];
27	  const width = Math.max(0.9, bodySize[0], headSize[0]);
28	  const headTop = bodySize[1] * 0.88 + headSize[1] * 0.5;
29	  const backgroundMaterial = new THREE.SpriteMaterial({ color: 0x1a0808, depthWrite: false });
30	  const fillMaterial = new THREE.SpriteMaterial({ color: 0x35d04f, depthWrite: false });
31	  const background = new THREE.Sprite(backgroundMaterial);
32	  const fill = new THREE.Sprite(fillMaterial);
33	  const group = new THREE.Group();
34	
35	  group.name = "hostile-health-bar";
36	  group.position.y = headTop + 0.35;
37	  background.name = "hostile-health-background";
38	  background.scale.set(width + 0.08, 0.18, 1);
39	  fill.name = "hostile-health-fill";
40	  fill.position.z = 0.001;
41	  fill.scale.set(width, 0.11, 1);
42	  group.add(background, fill);
43	
44	  return { group, fill, materials: [backgroundMaterial, fillMaterial], width };
45	}
46	
47	export function createMobVisuals(scene: THREE.Scene): MobVisuals {
48	  const visuals = new Map<number, MobVisual>();
49	  const seen = new Set<number>();
50	
51	  const removeModel = (id: number) => {
52	    const visual = visuals.get(id);
53	    if (!visual) return;
54	    scene.remove(visual.model.group);
55	    for (const material of visual.model.materials) material.dispose();
56	    for (const geometry of visual.model.geometries) geometry.dispose();
57	    for (const material of visual.healthBar?.materials ?? []) material.dispose();
58	    visuals.delete(id);
59	  };
60	
61	  return {
62	    sync(mobs, timeMs) {
63	      seen.clear();
64	      for (const mob of mobs) {
65	        seen.add(mob.id);
66	        let visual = visuals.get(mob.id);
67	        if (!visual) {
68	          const model = createMobModelForKind(mob.kind);
69	          const healthBar = mob.hostile ? createHealthBar(mob.kind) : null;
70	          if (healthBar) model.group.add(healthBar.group);
71	          visual = { model, healthBar };
72	          visuals.set(mob.id, visual);
73	          scene.add(model.group);
74	        }
75	        const { model, healthBar } = visual;
76	
77	        const bob = Math.sin(timeMs * 0.008 + mob.bobSeed) * 0.04;
78	        model.group.position.set(mob.position.x, mob.position.y + bob, mob.position.z);
79	        model.group.rotation.y = mob.yaw;
80	
81	        // A primed creeper swells and flashes white as its fuse burns down.
82	        let scale = mob.ageTimer > 0 ? BABY_SCALE : 1;
83	        if (mob.kind === "creeper") {
84	          const primed = (mob.fuseTimer ?? 0) > 0;
85	          const wave = 0.5 + 0.5 * Math.sin(timeMs * 0.025);
86	          if (primed) scale *= 1 + 0.18 * wave;
87	          const flash = primed ? 0.35 + 0.55 * wave : 0;
88	          for (const material of model.materials) (material as THREE.MeshStandardMaterial).emissive.setScalar(flash);
89	        }
90	        model.group.scale.setScalar(scale);
91	
92	        if (healthBar) {
93	          const hpPercent = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, mob.hp / MOB_TEMPLATES[mob.kind].hp));
94	          healthBar.fill.scale.x = healthBar.width * hpPercent;
95	          healthBar.fill.position.x = -(healthBar.width - healthBar.fill.scale.x) * 0.5;
96	        }
97	
98	        const gait = Math.sin(timeMs * 0.015 * mob.moveSpeed + mob.bobSeed) * 0.3;
99	        if (model.legs.length === 4) {
100	          model.legs[0].rotation.x = gait;
101	          model.legs[1].rotation.x = -gait;
102	          model.legs[2].rotation.x = -gait;
103	          model.legs[3].rotation.x = gait;
104	        }
105	      }
106	
107	      for (const id of visuals.keys()) {
108	        if (!seen.has(id)) removeModel(id);
109	      }
110	    },
111	
112	    dispose() {
113	      for (const id of [...visuals.keys()]) removeModel(id);
114	    }
115	  };
116	}
117
