Both ids exist in ITEM_DEFS already. */\nconst TAME_ITEMS: Partial<Record<MobKind, string>> = {\n  wolf: \"bone\",\n  cat: \"raw_fish\"\n};\n\n/**\n * Right-click an adult animal with its feed item to put it \"in love\" (toward\n * breeding). First in the right-click precedence so feeding wins over placing or\n * tilling when an animal is in the crosshair. Returns true when an animal was fed.\n */\nexport function tryFeedAimedMob(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent): boolean {\n  const slot = state.inventory[state.selectedSlot];\n  if (!slot?.id || slot.count <= 0) return false;\n  const index = findAimedMobIndex(state);\n  if (index < 0) return false;\n  const mob = state.mobs[index];\n  if (mob.hostile || FEED_ITEMS[mob.kind] !== slot.id) return false;\n  // A tameable kind only breeds once owned — a wild one is tamed (handled earlier\n  // in the precedence), never put \"in love\".\n  if (TAME_ITEMS[mob.kind] !== undefined && mob.owner == null) return false;\n  if (mob.ageTimer > 0 || mob.fedTimer > 0) return false; // babies and already-in-love animals decline\n\n  state.inventory = adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, slot.id, -1, state.selectedSlot) ?? state.inventory;\n  mob.fedTimer = BREED_FED_WINDOW_SECONDS;\n  emit({ type: \"mobFed\", kind: mob.kind });\n  return true;\n}\n\n/**\n * Right-click a WILD wolf/cat holding its treat (bone / raw fish) to attempt to\n * tame it. The treat is consumed whether or not the TAME_CHANCE roll succeeds (as\n * in Minecraft); on success the mob becomes an owned \"ally\" with boosted hp and an\n * enemy-detect range so it fights for the player. Runs before feeding/breeding in\n * the precedence so a bone tames a wild wolf rather than (no-op) feeding it.\n */\nexport function tryTameAimedMob(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent, rng: () => number): boolean {\n  const slot = state.inventory[state.selectedSlot];\n  if (!slot?.id || slot.count <= 0) return false;\n  const index = findAimedMobIndex(state);\n  if (index < 0) return false;\n  const mob = state.mobs[index];\n  if (mob.owner != null || TAME_ITEMS[mob.kind] !== slot.id) return false;\n\n  state.inventory = adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, slot.id, -1, state.selectedSlot) ?? state.inventory;\n  if (rng() < TAME_CHANCE) {\n    mob.owner = \"player\";\n    mob.faction = \"ally\";\n    mob.hp = PET_TAMED_HP;\n    mob.detectRange = PET_FIGHT_RANGE;\n    emit({ type: \"mobTamed\", kind: mob.kind, x: mob.position.x, y: mob.position.y, z: mob.position.z });\n  }\n  return true; // the treat is eaten either way\n}\n\n/**\n * Right-click your OWN pet (with anything that isn't its breeding treat) to toggle\n * its sit/stay. A sitting pet stays put — it won't follow, wander, or fight. Runs\n * after taming and feeding, so a treat still tames a wild one / breeds an owned one.\n */\nexport function tryToggleSitPet(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent): boolean {\n  const index = findAimedMobIndex(state);\n  if (index < 0) return false;\n  const mob = state.mobs[index];\n  if (mob.owner == null) return false; // only your own pet\n  mob.sitting = !mob.sitting;\n  emit({ type: \"petSitToggled\", kind: mob.kind, sitting: mob.sitting === true });\n  return true;\n}"
}

  "content": "import { describe, expect, test } from \"bun:test\";\nimport * as THREE from \"three\";\nimport { EYE_HEIGHT, PET_FIGHT_RANGE, PET_TAMED_HP } from \"@/lib/game/config\";\nimport { createEmptySlot, createSlot } from \"@/lib/game/items\";\nimport { countsById } from \"@/lib/game/inventory\";\nimport type { GameEvent, GameState, MobState } from \"@/lib/game/engine/state\";\nimport { tryTameAimedMob, tryToggleSitPet } from \"@/lib/game/engine/systems/interact\";\nimport type { InventorySlot, MobKind } from \"@/lib/game/types\";\n\nfunction inventory(items: Array<[string, number]>): InventorySlot[] {\n  const slots = Array.from({ length: 9 }, () => createEmptySlot());\n  items.forEach(([id, count], i) => (slots[i] = createSlot(id, count)));\n  return slots;\n}\n\nfunction makeState(slots: InventorySlot[], mob: MobState): GameState {\n  return {\n    player: { position: new THREE.Vector3(0, 64, 0), velocity: new THREE.Vector3(), yaw: 0, pitch: 0, onGround: true },\n    inventory: slots,\n    selectedSlot: 0,\n    mobs: [mob]\n  } as unknown as GameState;\n}\n\n/** A mob two blocks ahead (down -Z) at eye height — directly in the aim cone. */\nfunction mobInFront(kind: MobKind, overrides: Partial<MobState> = {}): MobState {\n  return {\n    kind,\n    hp: 8,\n    faction: \"wild\",\n    detectRange: 0,\n    position: new THREE.Vector3(0, 64 + EYE_HEIGHT, -2),\n    direction: new THREE.Vector3(),\n    ...overrides\n  } as unknown as MobState;\n}\n\ndescribe(\"tryTameAimedMob\", () => {\n  test(\"a successful roll tames a wild wolf: owner/faction/hp/range set, bone consumed, event fired\", () => {\n    const wolf = mobInFront(\"wolf\");\n    const state = makeState(inventory([[\"bone\", 2]]), wolf);\n    const events: GameEvent[] = [];\n\n    const consumed = tryTameAimedMob(state, (e) => events.push(e), () => 0); // 0 < TAME_CHANCE → success\n\n    expect(consumed).toBe(true);\n    expect(wolf.owner).toBe(\"player\");\n    expect(wolf.faction).toBe(\"ally\");\n    expect(wolf.hp).toBe(PET_TAMED_HP);\n    expect(wolf.detectRange).toBe(PET_FIGHT_RANGE);\n    expect(countsById(state.inventory).get(\"bone\") ?? 0).toBe(1); // one bone eaten\n    expect(events.some((e) => e.type === \"mobTamed\" && e.kind === \"wolf\")).toBe(true);\n  });\n\n  test(\"a failed roll still eats the treat but leaves the mob wild (consumes the click)\", () => {\n    const wolf = mobInFront(\"wolf\");\n    const state = makeState(inventory([[\"bone\", 1]]), wolf);\n    const events: GameEvent[] = [];\n\n    const consumed = tryTameAimedMob(state, (e) => events.push(e), () => 0.9); // 0.9 ≥ TAME_CHANCE → fail\n\n    expect(consumed).toBe(true);\n    expect(wolf.owner).toBeUndefined();\n    expect(countsById(state.inventory).get(\"bone\") ?? 0).toBe(0); // still eaten\n    expect(events.some((e) => e.type === \"mobTamed\")).toBe(false);\n  });\n\n  test(\"declines the wrong treat and an already-owned pet (no consumption)\", () => {\n    const wolfWrongTreat = mobInFront(\"wolf\");\n    const wrong = makeState(inventory([[\"wheat\", 1]]), wolfWrongTreat);\n    expect(tryTameAimedMob(wrong, () => {}, () => 0)).toBe(false);\n    expect(countsById(wrong.inventory).get(\"wheat\") ?? 0).toBe(1);\n\n    const ownedWolf = mobInFront(\"wolf\", { owner: \"player\", faction: \"ally\" });\n    const owned = makeState(inventory([[\"bone\", 1]]), ownedWolf);\n    expect(tryTameAimedMob(owned, () => {}, () => 0)).toBe(false);\n    expect(countsById(owned.inventory).get(\"bone\") ?? 0).toBe(1);\n  });\n});\n\ndescribe(\"tryToggleSitPet\", () => {\n  test(\"toggles sit on your own pet and fires the event\", () => {\n    const pet = mobInFront(\"wolf\", { owner: \"player\", faction: \"ally\" });\n    const state = makeState(inventory([[\"diamond_sword\", 1]]), pet);\n    const events: GameEvent[] = [];\n\n    expect(tryToggleSitPet(state, (e) => events.push(e))).toBe(true);\n    expect(pet.sitting).toBe(true);\n    expect(events.some((e) => e.type === \"petSitToggled\" && e.sitting === true)).toBe(true);\n\n    expect(tryToggleSitPet(state, () => {})).toBe(true);\n    expect(pet.sitting).toBe(false); // toggles back\n  });\n\n  test(\"declines a mob you don't own\", () => {\n    const wild = mobInFront(\"wolf\");\n    const state = makeState(inventory([[\"diamond_sword\", 1]]), wild);\n    expect(tryToggleSitPet(state, () => {})).toBe(false);\n    expect(wild.sitting).toBeUndefined();\n  });\n});\n"
}

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	### Added
8	
9	- **Advancements & statistics**: the game gains a progression meta — running **statistics** (blocks mined, monsters slain, items crafted/enchanted, potions drunk, fish caught, animals bred, distance travelled, time played, deaths, jumps, villager trades) and a tight, flat set of **16 advancements**, one per major system (mine a log/stone/sliver/diamond, craft a pickaxe, craft a furnace, fire a bow, slay a hostile, defeat the Dragon Lord, breed animals, harvest wheat, catch a fish, enchant an item, drink a potion, sleep, trade with a villager). All on **zero new assets** — advancement icons reuse existing item/block sprites — and the save schema bumps **v12 → v13** (additive), with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
10	  - Press **L** to open a dedicated two-tab overlay (mutually exclusive with the inventory; the pause menu won't open over it): an **Advancements** grid grouped by category with locked/unlocked styling, and a **Statistics** list of the counters. Each unlock raises an _"Advancement Unlocked"_ toast and a celebratory chime
11	  - **Persist across death.** Like `xp` and unlike status `effects`, both stats and advancements are a long-term record that survives a death (`clearEffects` never touches them) and a reload
12	  - **Architecture**: one observer at the engine's single `emit` chokepoint folds every gameplay event into the stat counters (`recordEvent`), then unlocks any advancement whose threshold the new stats just crossed and announces it (`advancementUnlocked` event) — no per-system bookkeeping. The whole set is a **declarative registry** in `lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts` (`{ stat, threshold }` per row), so `evaluateAdvancements` is pure and adding one is a one-line edit. A new broadly-useful `crafted` event drives the craft/brew/trade counters; `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS` (`lib/game/mobs.ts`) is the single source of truth for counting hostile kills. The overlay reads detail through a new `GameApi.advancementState()` pulled on render, so play never churns the snapshot with stat values the HUD doesn't show
13	
14	## [0.11.0] - 2026-06-28
15	
16	### Fixed
17	
18	- **Equipped armor no longer occupies a hotbar/inventory slot.** Armor was equipped _by reference_ — the worn piece stayed in the inventory and kept occupying its slot (and rendered twice: once in the hotbar/grid, once in the armor column). Armor now has **dedicated storage**: equipping **moves** the piece out of the inventory into its armor slot (freeing the slot, ending the double-render), and unequipping returns it to a free inventory slot (refused when the inventory is full, so nothing is lost). `EquippedArmor` now holds the worn `InventorySlot` instances; the defense/durability/Mending seams read them directly (no more find-by-id, which also removes the duplicate-piece ambiguity). The save schema bumps **v11 → v12** — `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName) — with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
19	
20	### Added
21	
22	- **Three new potions — Haste, Resistance & Leaping**: brewed at the brewing stand from existing reagents (Gold Ore / Leather / Sliver Ore), on **zero new assets** and **no save-format or worldgen change**. **Haste** (`EFFECT_HASTE_MULTIPLIER` 1.4) speeds up mining (`mining.ts`); **Resistance** (`EFFECT_RESISTANCE_MULTIPLIER` 0.8) softens incoming **combat** damage only — lava/poison/void are untouched — at the `applyDamageWithArmor` seam; **Leaping** (Jump Boost, `EFFECT_JUMP_BOOST_VELOCITY` 2.0) raises the jump in `playerMotion.ts` (tuned to stay under the fall-damage threshold). Each is an engine-only buff with a procedurally-painted HUD icon (no renderer change); the three effect ids ride the existing top-level `effects` field (added to `VALID_EFFECT_IDS`), so no save bump
23	- **Tool & armor enchantments — Fortune & Feather Falling**: on **zero new assets** and **no save-format or worldgen change**. **Fortune** (tools) rolls up to `FORTUNE_BONUS_PER_LEVEL` (1) extra of an **ore** per level when you mine it (gated to the ore blocks in `rollBlockDrops`, read off the mining tool). **Feather Falling** (boots only, via the `itemIds` allow-list) cuts fall damage by `FEATHER_FALLING_REDUCE_PER_LEVEL` (0.15) per level — capped at `FEATHER_FALLING_MAX_REDUCTION` (0.8) — read off the worn boots at the `tickPlayerMotion` fall seam. Both ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` (added to `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS`), so no save bump
24	- **Weapon enchantments — Knockback & Looting**: two new enchantments for any weapon, on **zero new assets** and **no save-format or worldgen change**. **Knockback** adds `KNOCKBACK_PER_LEVEL` (0.4) to the melee shove per level (the base shove is now the named `MELEE_KNOCKBACK_IMPULSE` (0.75), no longer a magic number), read off the held weapon at the `tryAttackMob` seam. **Looting** rolls up to `LOOTING_BONUS_PER_LEVEL` (1) extra of each mob drop per level on a **melee** kill (the killing weapon's level is forwarded through the kill callback, so arrows/thrown spears/explosions apply none), in `rollMobDrops`. Both ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` (added to `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS`), so no save bump
25	- **Bow enchantments — Power & Punch**: two new enchantments for the existing enchanting table, on **zero new assets** and **no save-format or worldgen change**. **Power** adds `POWER_DAMAGE_PER_LEVEL` (2) arrow damage per level and **Punch** adds `PUNCH_KNOCKBACK_PER_LEVEL` (0.25) arrow knockback per level, both read off the held bow at the single `tryFireBow` seam. They're **bow-only**: `EnchantmentDef` gains an optional `itemIds` allow-list (`canEnchant` honors it on top of the item-kind gate), so these don't appear on swords (which are also `weapon`). Their ids ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` (added to `VALID_ENCHANT_IDS`), so no save bump (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
26	- **Equipped armor now shows on the player** in third-person (press **V**). Each worn piece renders as a procedurally-built voxel "shell" over the matching body part (helmet → head, face mask → visor, neck protection → collar, chestplate → torso + shoulder caps, leggings → upper legs, boots → feet), parented to the limb pivots so it animates with the walk/attack gait, and tinted toward the ore it's crafted from. Renderer-only (`playerModel.ts` builds the shells, `playerVisuals.ts` toggles each by what's worn) — zero new assets, no engine/save change
27	- **Grindstone**: a new crafted station (**2 cobble + 2 planks**) — the anvil's inverse, on **zero new assets** (a procedurally-painted stone-wheel block, reusing existing synth) and **no save-format or worldgen change**. Right-click to open the grindstone panel; with **enchanted** gear selected in the hotbar, **Remove enchantments** strips them all and refunds **`GRINDSTONE_REFUND_XP_PER_LEVEL` (5) XP per level** removed. Pure logic in `lib/game/grindstone.ts`, a new `grindstoneStrip` command, and a `GrindstoneColumn` panel; the `Grindstone` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 54), craft-only, so no worldgen baseline change
28	- **Anvil**: a new crafted station (**3 gold ore + 4 cobble**) for maintaining and consolidating gear, on **zero new assets** (a procedurally-painted dark-iron block, reusing existing synth for its clang). The save schema bumps **v10 → v11** (additive `customName`), with **no worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8)
29	  - Right-click to open the anvil panel, which — like the enchanting table — acts on the **selected hotbar** tool/weapon/armor and spends XP levels. Three actions: **Combine** a duplicate (adds the two durability bars + a bonus and **merges enchantments** at the higher level, consuming the duplicate); **Repair** with the item's tier material (e.g. diamond ore for a diamond sword, cobble for a stone pickaxe) for a chunk of durability without a second copy; and **Rename** (the custom name shows everywhere the item's label does)
30	  - **Architecture**: the new `Anvil` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 53) so saved block ids never shift, and it's craft-only so no worldgen baseline changes. Pure logic lives in `lib/game/anvil.ts` (`combineSlots`, `mergeEnchantments`, `findSacrificeIndex`, `materialRepair`, `sanitizeCustomName`), driven by new `anvilCombine`/`anvilRepair`/`anvilRename` commands. The anvil station id is threaded through the **engine/UI** `craftingStation` union only (not `Recipe.station`); the panel is a new `AnvilColumn`. A per-item `customName` (additive v11 field, durable gear only, trimmed + capped) persists the rename, surfaced everywhere via a shared `displayName` helper

39:### Version history
41:- **v13** (advancements & statistics) — adds optional top-level `stats` (`{ id, value }[]`) and `advancements` (`string[]`). `migrateSaveV12toV13` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ no stats, no advancements yet earned). Both are progression meta folded in at the engine's single emit chokepoint and, like `xp` and **unlike `effects`**, are **kept across death** (`clearEffects` never touches them). `serializeStats`/`restoreStats` and `restoreAdvancements` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. No new `BlockId`, no new item, and no worldgen change — advancement icons reuse existing item/block sprites — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
42:- **Unreleased (no save bump)** — new enchantments (**Power**, **Punch**, **Knockback**, **Looting**, **Fortune**, **Feather Falling**) ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` field, and new status effects (**Haste**, **Resistance**, **Jump Boost**) ride the existing top-level `effects` field. Their ids are added to the save validators' known-id sets (`VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` / `VALID_EFFECT_IDS`, both compile-enforced `Record<…, true>`). No new field, no new `BlockId`, no worldgen change — the save schema stays **v12** and **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** (the same additive-id pattern as Mending). Older builds silently drop unknown ids on load.
43:- **v12** (dedicated armor storage) — fixes a bug where equipped armor stayed in the inventory and occupied a hotbar/storage slot. `equippedArmor` is no longer a by-id reference into `inventorySlots` but the worn pieces themselves, persisted per slot as `SavedSlot` (via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`, reusing the shared `restoreSlot` validation). `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName; equips whose item isn't found or isn't valid armor are dropped; a legacy `inventoryCounts`-only save just drops the equip map and keeps the items). No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
44:- **v11** (anvil rename & Mending) — adds an optional `customName` on each `SavedSlot` (the anvil rename). `migrateSaveV10toV11` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no custom name). `customName` rides the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests), is restored on durable gear only, and is trimmed + capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN` with blanks dropped. The **Mending** enchantment adds no new field — it rides the existing per-slot `enchantments` (and its `mending` id is added to the save validator's known-id set). The **Anvil** and **Grindstone** items save by string id and their `BlockId`s are **appended** so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — both are craft-only — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
45:- **v10** (Hardcore) — adds optional top-level `hardcore` and `gameOver` booleans. `migrateSaveV9toV10` is a pure version bump (both absent ⇒ a normal, non-hardcore world, via `restoreHardcore`/`restoreGameOver`). `hardcore` is immutable (forces Survival + Hard, locks both switchers); `gameOver` is the persisted permadeath flag, so a dead hardcore world reloads into its spectator state rather than respawning (the transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` remain session-only). No worldgen change — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
46:- **v9** (difficulty) — adds an optional top-level `difficulty` (`"peaceful"` | `"easy"` | `"normal"` | `"hard"`). `migrateSaveV8toV9` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ `"normal"`, via `restoreDifficulty`). Difficulty is an axis orthogonal to `gameMode`, switchable in-game, so the _current_ level is what's stored; the per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts` and the `starvationTimer` accumulator is session-only. No worldgen change — difficulty touches no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
47:- **v8** (game modes) — adds an optional top-level `gameMode` (`"survival"` | `"creative"` | `"adventure"` | `"spectator"`). `migrateSaveV7toV8` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ `"survival"`, via `restoreGameMode`). The mode is switchable in-game, so the _current_ mode is what's stored; the transient `isFlying` is never serialized. No worldgen change — modes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
48:- **v7** (XP & enchanting) — adds optional top-level `xp` and an optional `enchantments` array on each `SavedSlot`. `migrateSaveV6toV7` is a pure version bump (absent → xp 0, no enchantments). XP persists and is **kept across death** (it's a currency, not a status effect); enchantments ride the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests) and are validated on load. The **Enchanting Table** item saves by string id and the `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 52) so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
49:- **v6** (status effects, brewing & potions) — adds optional `effects` (`{ id, remaining }[]`). `migrateSaveV5toV6` is a pure version bump (absent → no active effects), so pre-effect saves load clean. Effects persist but are cleared on death; `serializeEffects`/`restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. Potions, glass bottles, and the **Brewing Stand** item save by string id; the `BrewingStand` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 51) so existing saved block ids never shift, and a placed stand persists in the block diff like any block. No worldgen change — the new effects/recipes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and the determinism hashes are untouched.
50:- **v5** (unchanged for fishing) — the active cast is the session-only `state.fishing` field (a transient bobber, like in-flight arrows and thrown spears); it is never serialized and is cleared on respawn. The fishing rod and raw/cooked fish are additive items saved by string id, and a catch is an ordinary inventory change. No worldgen change, so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved.
51:- **v5** (unchanged for the living world — saplings, bone meal & grass spread) — every effect is an ordinary block edit that rides the `changes` diff: a planted sapling, a grown tree's wood and leaves, and re-grassed dirt all persist with no new fields, and bone meal is an additive item saved by string id. The `Sapling` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 50) so existing saved block ids never shift. Crucially, the runtime tree grower (`systems/treeGrowth.ts`) shares **no** code with worldgen's hash-pinned `placeTrees`, so the generated terrain is byte-identical and **neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved**.
52:- **v5** (unchanged for villagers & trading) — the villager mob is transient like every mob, and trading needs no persisted state: a trade is a station-gated recipe (`station: "villager"`) run through the existing `craft` command, the open trade station (`craftingStation`) is session-only, and there are no per-trade use caps to store. **Emerald** and any traded goods save by string id in the existing inventory slots. No worldgen change (villagers spawn into the passive population; there are no village structures), so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved.
53:- **v5** (unchanged for creepers & TNT) — the creeper mob, gunpowder, and the explosion system add no persisted state: mobs are transient, **a creeper's lit fuse and a primed TNT block's countdown are session-only** (`MobState.fuseTimer` and `state.primedTnt` are never serialized — like the boss and in-flight arrows). Gunpowder and the TNT item save by string id; a **placed TNT block persists in the block diff** like any block, and a save written mid-fuse reloads with that TNT as an inert, un-lit block (and no creeper). There is no worldgen change — creepers are spawned and TNT is crafted — so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved. Blast-destroyed blocks are ordinary block-diff edits.
54:- **v5** (unchanged for cow/pig & coal) — the cow and pig mobs (and their meat/leather drops) add no persisted state; mobs are transient and the new foods save by string id. Coal ore, coal, and charcoal are likewise additive (the ore persists in the block diff, the items by string id), so the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the new coal worldgen changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` is bumped `7` → `8`**: a world whose recorded version differs discards its stale block-diffs and reboots from its seed. Coal runs on its own PRNG (`placeCoal`), so only underground coal cells differ from a v7 world — the surface, existing ores, trees, and structures are byte-identical (the meshing and structural-probe tests stay green; only the byte hashes were re-rolled).
55:- **v5** (unchanged for caves & lighting) — the lighting system adds no persisted state (light is a derived cache, recomputed at load), and lava is worldgen, not a saved field. So the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`**: old block-diffs were computed against the lava-free world and must never be applied to the new one. Pre-lava saves are discarded in practice. Torches are additive items/blocks, persisted by string id / in the block diff like any other placed block.
56:- **v5** (unchanged for ranged combat & the endgame boss) — bows, arrows, the Cursed Totem, the Dragon Heart, and the Dragon Sword are **additive items**, persisted by string id in the existing inventory/container slots, so no schema change was needed. **Arrows in flight, the boss, its minions, and the `victory` flag are all transient** (never serialized — like mobs), and there is no worldgen change (the boss is summoned, not generated), so neither the `version` nor `SAVE_KEY` moved.
57:- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5 → v6 → v7 → v8 → v9 → v10 → v11 → v12 → v13.
58:- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.
59:- **v3** — adds optional `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger`, and `spawnPoint`. `migrateSaveV2toV3` is a pure version bump (the new fields stay absent and restore as engine defaults), so **`SAVE_KEY` is unchanged** and v1/v2 saves load fine.
62:- Unknown future versions are rejected (treated as no save).
64:## Profiles & worlds
66:Saves are organized two levels deep — a **profile** owns a list of **worlds**, and each world holds one `SaveData` blob — across three localStorage keys. All three are versioned `{ version: 1, ... }` envelopes and their readers are **total** (malformed entries are dropped, never thrown):
72:`worldgenVersion` records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (`lib/game/config.ts`, currently 8) the world was generated under. This **replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump**: when the worldgen baseline changes, bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, and a world whose recorded version differs has its stale block-diffs discarded and reboots from its stored seed — per-world, with no key rename and without touching unaffected worlds.
74:**World types.** A world's `worldType` selects a generation preset (`lib/world/worldTypes.ts`). `generateWorld(world, worldType)` forks on it before any block write (`terrainConfigFor`, `lib/world/generation.ts`), varying only sea level and per-biome surface height; everything else reads `GEN`. The `"default"` branch returns the GEN values verbatim, so default worlds stay **byte-identical** to the pre-feature generator — the existing determinism hashes are unchanged. Each non-default type is its own deterministic save contract with its own SHA-256 baseline in `generation.test.ts`; `worldgenVersion` still guards all types (a deliberate change to any type's config bumps `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, discarding stale worlds of that vintage).
78:### Legacy migration

86:## Compatibility rules
88:- Saves store **diffs against generated terrain**, so changing world generation or the voxel index formula (`x + z*sizeX + y*sizeX*sizeZ`) silently corrupts existing saves — bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` when you do, and each world discards its stale diffs (rebooting from its seed) on the mismatch.
89:- Worldgen output is pinned by SHA-256 characterization tests in `lib/world/generation.test.ts`; they fail on any byte-level change. See [testing.md](testing.md) for the re-baseline policy. Caveat: the noise functions use `Math.sin`, whose exact results are engine-defined — the tests prove refactor purity on the pinned Bun version, not cross-browser save portability.
90:- Changing the save shape requires bumping the `version` field and handling (or discarding) old data. Round-trip tests live in `lib/game/save.test.ts` and `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.test.ts`.

3	## Schema
4	
5	`SaveData` (version 13) in `lib/game/types.ts`:
6	
7	- world `seed`
8	- `worldType` (optional) — the generation preset (`"default"` | `"flat"` | `"amplified"` | `"islands"`); absent ⇒ `"default"`. Like `seed`, it is fixed for the world's life and the world must always regenerate with it, since the block-diffs were recorded against that terrain
9	- `gameMode` (optional) — the player's game mode (`"survival"` | `"creative"` | `"adventure"` | `"spectator"`); absent ⇒ `"survival"`. Unlike `worldType`, this is **switchable in-game** (pause menu), so the saved value is the _current_ mode, not the one chosen at creation. Restored by `restoreGameMode` (`lib/game/save.ts`); `isFlying` is session-only and never serialized
10	- `difficulty` (optional) — the player's difficulty (`"peaceful"` | `"easy"` | `"normal"` | `"hard"`); absent ⇒ `"normal"`. An axis orthogonal to `gameMode`, and likewise **switchable in-game** (pause menu), so the saved value is the _current_ difficulty. Restored by `restoreDifficulty` (`lib/game/save.ts`); the per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts`, the starvation accumulator (`starvationTimer`) is session-only
11	- `hardcore` (optional) — the Hardcore flag (`boolean`); absent ⇒ `false`. **Immutable** (unlike `gameMode`/`difficulty`): a hardcore world is forced to Survival + Hard and the engine locks both switchers. Restored by `restoreHardcore`
12	- `gameOver` (optional) — the permadeath flag (`boolean`); absent ⇒ `false`. Set once a hardcore run has ended in death; a reloaded `gameOver` world boots into the spectator "dead world" state (never playable). Restored by `restoreGameOver`. (The transient `isDead`/`respawnTimer` stay session-only — hardcore death is captured by this flag instead.)
13	- a block **diff** list — `changes: [blockIndex, blockId][]`; edits that revert to the generated baseline are pruned (player-placed crops, beds, furnaces, chests, and both halves/states of doors ride this list — they are ordinary block edits)
14	- inventory slots with durability, **enchantments, and a custom name** (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar). Each `SavedSlot` is `{ id, count, durability?, enchantments?, customName? }`; `enchantments` (`{ id, level }[]`) and `customName` (the anvil rename) ride durable gear only and are validated on load (`restoreSlot` — known enchant ids via `Object.hasOwn`, levels clamped to `1..ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL`; `customName` trimmed and capped to `CUSTOM_NAME_MAX_LEN`, blanks dropped). The same path serializes chest contents
15	- `xp` (optional) — banked experience points (`XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level). Earned from kills/ore/fishing, spent at the enchanting table. Restored by `restoreXp` (finite, ≥ 0). Unlike effects, XP is a currency and is **kept across death**
16	- equipped armor — the worn pieces themselves (one per slot, dedicated storage), persisted as per-slot `SavedSlot` via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor` (so worn durability/enchantments/customName survive). A worn piece lives **only** here, not in the 36 inventory slots
17	- selected hotbar slot (0–8)
18	- player position — validated on load by `restorePlayerPosition` (`lib/game/save.ts`): coords keep their fractional part (the player isn't grid-aligned) but a missing or non-finite (NaN/Infinity) position is rejected, leaving the fresh spawn in place so a corrupt blob can't load a broken world or slip past the `position.y < 2` unstuck net
19	- `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger` (all optional) — time of day and player stats, so sleeping through the night and a hurt/hungry player survive a reload
20	- `spawnPoint` (optional, `{x,y,z}` or null) — the bed respawn point; respawn falls back to a random land point when it is null or the block there is no longer a bed
21	- `blockEntities` (optional) — chest contents as `{ index, slots }[]`, keyed by the block's voxel index (the same index space as `changes`). Only **non-empty** chests are stored; an empty one carries no data and is recreated empty when opened. On load each entry is kept only if that index still holds a Chest block. This is the first per-block metadata in the format — `lib/game/save.ts` (`serializeContainers` / `readContainers`) handles it
22	- `effects` (optional) — active status effects as `{ id, remaining }[]` (remaining in seconds). Drink-granted buffs (Speed/Strength/Regeneration/Fire Resistance/Water Breathing) and the rotten-flesh Poison hazard live in `state.effects` (a Map) and persist here, but are **cleared on death**, so a saved-then-reloaded world resumes whatever was active at save time. On load, `restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) drops unknown ids and non-positive/garbage durations
23	- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of dungeon loot chests the player has already opened or broken. Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only set of _which_ indices are dungeon chests/spawners is not stored; it is re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`
24	- `stats` (optional) — gameplay **statistics** as `{ id, value }[]` (blocks mined, mobs killed, items crafted/enchanted, potions drunk, fish caught, distance travelled, time played, …). Counters live in `state.stats` (a `Map<string, number>`) and are folded in at the engine's single emit chokepoint (`recordEvent`/`recordTick`, `lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts`). Like `xp` and **unlike `effects`**, they are a long-term record and are **kept across death**. Only positive values are written; `restoreStats` (`lib/game/save.ts`) drops non-string ids and negative/garbage values. The id set is open (per-recipe `crafted_<id>` and per-block `*_mined` counters), so there's no allow-list
25	- `advancements` (optional) — the unlocked **advancement** ids as `string[]`. Unlock is uniform — `state.stats.get(stat) >= threshold` for each declarative entry in `ADVANCEMENTS` (`lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts`) — and ids accumulate in `state.advancements` (a `Set`). Also **kept across death**; `restoreAdvancements` (`lib/game/save.ts`) keeps non-empty strings only, de-duplicated. Unknown persisted ids (e.g. a renamed entry) are harmless: they round-trip but never re-unlock, since `evaluateAdvancements` only iterates the registry
26	
27	Each world's `SaveData` is stored in its own localStorage key, `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` (`worldSaveKey` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`). Read/write and restore validation live in `lib/game/save.ts` — `readSave`/`writeSave` take the key as a parameter and the `Storage` is injectable for tests; `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff. (The legacy single-world key `SAVE_KEY` = `minecraft_save_v7` is now read only once, by the migration described under [Profiles & worlds](#profiles--worlds).)
28	
29	Audio volume preferences live under a **separate**, global key (`minecraft_audio_v1`, `lib/game/audio/settings.ts`), shared across all profiles and not part of any world save or its versioning.
30	
```

Right-click one holding its treat — a\n**Bone** for a wolf, **Raw Fish** for a cat — to attempt to tame it; the treat is\neaten whether or not the ~1-in-3 roll succeeds. A tamed pet becomes your **ally**:\n\n- **Fights for you** — it attacks nearby hostiles (within ~12 blocks) on its own, and its kills drop loot and XP straight to you.\n- **Follows you** — it roams near you, jogs to catch up when it strays, and is recalled (teleported) to your side if it gets more than ~24 blocks away.\n- **Sit / stay** — right-click your own pet (holding anything that isn't its breeding treat) to toggle sitting; a sitting pet stays put and won't follow or fight.\n- **Persists** — pets are the only mobs saved with the world; they (and their bred offspring) survive a reload.\n\nMobs also now fight **each other**: hostiles hunt villagers (who flee), and your pets defend against them. Mob-vs-mob combat is melee-only."

198	### Combat
199	
200	Hold **left-click** to swing. You hit a mob if it's within **~4.5 blocks** and
201	close to your crosshair (a fairly tight aim cone). Bare fists do **6 damage**;
202	weapons do much more and have durability that ticks down with each hit. A landed
203	blow knocks the mob back.
204	
205	Spears trade a little melee damage for **~7-block reach**. With a spear selected,
206	press **`E`** or right-click to throw it: the projectile follows an arc, stops on
207	the first mob it hits, and costs one durability. A missed spear embeds in terrain
208	for two seconds before disappearing. The spear remains in your inventory until
209	its durability runs out. Armor, tools, knives, swords, and spears never stack;
210	every durable item occupies its own slot.
211	
212	**Armor** reduces incoming damage. Click a helmet, face mask, neck protection,
213	chestplate, leggings, or boots in your inventory to **equip** it — the piece
214	**moves into its dedicated armor slot** (on the left of the inventory), freeing the
215	inventory/hotbar slot it came from. Click the armor slot to take it back off (it
216	returns to a free inventory slot). Each piece adds defense and absorbs durability
217	when you're struck — but a hit always deals at least **1 damage**, even in a full set.
218	Worn pieces also **show on your character** in third-person (press **V**), each tinted
219	toward the ore it's made from.
220	
221	**Ranged combat.** Craft a **bow** (3 wood + 3 string) and **arrows** (1 stone +
222	1 wood + 1 feather makes 4). With the bow selected, **left-click fires an arrow**
223	along your aim — arrows arc with gravity, so lead distant or moving targets and
224	aim a little high. Each shot spends one arrow and a little bow durability. Watch
225	out: **skeletons now shoot back**, keeping their distance and firing arrows, so
226	use cover and close the gap or out-shoot them.
227

228	## Day, night, and danger
229	
230	A full day lasts **240 seconds (4 minutes)**. Daylight rises and falls on a smooth
231	curve from ~0.04 at midnight to ~1.0 at noon. Three thresholds matter:
232	
233	| Daylight       | What happens                                                              |
234	| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
235	| below **0.28** | Night: hostile mobs spawn, and you may sleep                              |
236	| below **0.42** | Spiders turn hostile (they're passive in twilight and day)                |
237	| above **0.72** | Hostile mobs caught in open sunlight catch fire and burn (caves are safe) |
238	
239	The game boots at a dim dawn, so the very first mobs can already be active —
240	build or sleep quickly.
241	
242	**Weather and sky.** It periodically **rains** — or **snows** up in the mountains —
243	with clouds rolling in, the sky greying over, and the light dimming; deserts and
244	oceans stay clear. At night the sky fills with **stars and a moon**, while clouds
245	drift overhead by day. Weather is atmospheric only: it doesn't change how mobs
246	spawn or behave, and it isn't saved.
247	
248	## Mining and building
249	
250	**Break** a block by holding left-click; a crack overlay shows progress, and harder
251	blocks take longer. **Place** the selected hotbar item with right-click (or `E`)
252	against a surface. Your reach is about **7 blocks**.
253	
254	**Tools gate what you can mine.** A pickaxe's tier determines which blocks it can
255	harvest at all — mining with too weak a tool yields nothing:
256	
257	| To mine…                  | You need at least… |

The fungible wild/hostile population is re-seeded each boot, so don't persist it (it would just duplicate).\n- **A new `MobKind` touches six exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables** (typecheck enforces all of them): `MOB_TEMPLATES` + `FACTION_BY_KIND` (`mobs.ts`), `MOB_DROPS` (`mobLoot.ts`), `MOB_XP` (`mobXp.ts`), `CALL_INTERVALS` (`mobAmbience.ts`), and `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS` + `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS` (`soundParams.ts`). Also decide its `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS` membership (`mobs.ts`). `soundParams.test.ts` iterates `MOB_TEMPLATES`, so the sound/template tables stay in lockstep."
}

Done — **PR-A is built, pushed, and opened as [hutusi/monecraft#39](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/pull/39)**.

## What shipped (PR-A — "Living mobs & companions")

Four focused commits, save **v13→v14**, worldgen unchanged, zero new assets:

1. **Allegiance + mob-vs-mob combat** — a `faction` axis (wild/hostile/ally/villager/raider) alongside the existing `hostile` flag, a shared enmity table, and throttled target selection. Hostiles now hunt **villagers** (who flee); kills credit loot/XP by the *victim's* faction. Mob-vs-mob is melee-only and uses raw damage.
2. **Mob persistence (v13→v14)** — the first time any mob is saved. `SavedMob` + `serializeMobs`/`restoreMobs`; only tamed pets persist (the wild population re-seeds each boot, so persisting it would double it).
3. **Tameable wolf & cat** — feed a bone/raw fish to tame (~1-in-3); a pet follows, **sits/stays**, **fights hostiles for you**, teleports back if it strays, and persists (offspring inherit ownership).
4. **Docs + CHANGELOG + e2e** bump.

## Verification
Full gate green: lint, typecheck, format, **926 unit tests**, build, and **18 e2e** (incl. the v14 save assertion). One caveat — the visuals/audio that can't be checked headless (wolf/cat look, sit pose, tame hearts, bark/meow) want a **manual `bun run dev` pass before you merge**.

## Next — PR-B (villages, professions, raids)
Per the plan, **PR-B branches off PR-A's *merged* `main`** (it depends on the v14 `mobs` field), so it shouldn't start until #39 lands. And when I do build it, I'll **hold it locally for your review before any push**, as you asked.

So the ball's in your court: review/merge #39 (a manual gameplay pass first is wise), and once it's on `main`, tell me to start PR-B. Want me to do anything else on PR-A in the meantime?

export function tryToggleSitPet(state: GameState, emit: EmitGameEvent): boolean {
  const slot = state.inventory[state.selectedSlot];
  const index = findAimedMobIndex(state);
  if (index < 0) return false;
  const mob = state.mobs[index];
  if (mob.owner == null) return false; // only your own pet
  if (slot?.id && FEED_ITEMS[mob.kind] === slot.id) return false;
  mob.sitting = !mob.sitting;
  emit({ type: "petSitToggled", kind: mob.kind, sitting: mob.sitting === true });
```

  "old_string": "/** Nearest hostile/raider within `range` of a villager (drives its flee), or null. */\nfunction nearestThreat(state: GameState, mob: MobState, range: number): MobState | null {\n  let best: MobState | null = null;\n  let bestSq = range * range;\n  for (const other of state.mobs) {\n    if (other.hp <= 0 || !THREAT_FACTIONS.has(other.faction)) continue;\n    const d = horizDistSq(mob, other);\n    if (d < bestSq) {\n      bestSq = d;\n      best = other;\n    }\n  }\n  return best;\n}",
  "new_string": "/** Nearest hostile/raider within `range` of a villager (drives its flee), or null. */\nfunction nearestThreat(state: GameState, mob: MobState, range: number): MobState | null {\n  let best: MobState | null = null;\n  let bestSq = range * range;\n  for (const other of state.mobs) {\n    if (other.hp <= 0 || !THREAT_FACTIONS.has(other.faction)) continue;\n    const d = horizDistSq(mob, other);\n    if (d < bestSq) {\n      bestSq = d;\n      best = other;\n    }\n  }\n  return best;\n}\n\n/** True when nothing solid blocks the segment from a fighter's eye to its target — so it can't bite through a wall/door. */\nfunction mobVsMobLineOfSight(world: GameState[\"world\"], mob: MobState, dx: number, dy: number, dz: number): boolean {\n  scratchRay.set(dx, dy, dz);\n  if (scratchRay.lengthSq() <= 1e-6) return true;\n  const dist = scratchRay.length();\n  scratchMobEye.set(mob.position.x, mob.position.y + mob.halfHeight * 0.35, mob.position.z);\n  return voxelRaycast(world, scratchMobEye, scratchRay.normalize(), dist) === null;\n}"
}

Also decide its `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS` membership (`mobs.ts`). `soundParams.test.ts` iterates `MOB_TEMPLATES`, so the sound/template tables stay in lockstep.
docs/architecture.md:60:**Endgame boss & victory.** A `"boss"` `MobKind` is summoned from a held Cursed Totem via a step in the `placeBlock` precedence (`GameEngine.trySummonBoss`, which seeds placement and refuses if a boss already exists). Defeating it (`removeMobAt`) drops a Dragon Heart, sets the session-only `state.victory`, and emits `bossDefeated`. Boss HP, player-relative bearing, horizontal block distance, and the victory flag reach React through `GameSnapshot.boss`/`victory`; the `boss` object is rebuilt only when one of its rounded visible values changes, avoiding sub-block React churn. Renderer-side hostile health bars are procedural `THREE.Sprite`s attached to each mob model and updated directly from `MobState.hp`, so ordinary mob damage does not enter the React snapshot. A new `"boss"` kind requires entries in all five exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables (`MOB_TEMPLATES`, `MOB_DROPS`, `CALL_INTERVALS`, `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS`, `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS`).
CHANGELOG.md:100:  - **Architecture**: a trade is simply a **`station: "villager"` recipe** (`lib/game/trades.ts`, spread into `RECIPES`), so it reuses the entire crafting pipeline and recipe-book UI — opening a villager just sets `craftingStation = "villager"`, and the existing `craft` command runs the trade. The new `"villager"` `MobKind` fills all five exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables. **No save-format or worldgen change**: villagers are transient, the open trade station is session-only, there are no per-trade use caps to persist, and emerald/traded items save by string id. (Village _structures_ are a possible future addition — villagers currently wander the world among the existing houses rather than spawning in generated settlements, which keeps this change off the worldgen-determinism baseline.)
CHANGELOG.md:106:  - The new `"creeper"` `MobKind` fills all five exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables. Explosions drive a procedural fireball + smoke burst and a synthesized boom; a primed creeper swells and flashes via its `MobState.fuseTimer`. **No save-format or worldgen change**: creepers are spawned, TNT is crafted, fuses are transient, and the new items save by string id
CHANGELOG.md:156:  - New `"boss"` `MobKind` touches all five exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables (templates, drops, ambience intervals, ambient + attack sounds). New events (`arrowHit`, `bowFired`, `bossSummoned`, `bossDefeated`, `summonFailed`) drive procedural impact sparks, a conjuring column, a victory burst, and synthesized bow-twang / arrow-tick / boss-roar / victory-fanfare sounds. In-flight arrows render as a pooled extruded-sprite mesh (one shared geometry/material) oriented along their velocity

## CodeRabbit review on #39 — 10 findings, all addressed

CI was already green (verify, e2e, CodeRabbit all pass); these were code-quality/correctness comments. No human review yet — CodeRabbit is the only reviewer.

**Major (3):**
| Finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| Pets were **XP-farmable** — a credited kill awards `xpForMob`, so you could kill your own pet for XP | Set wolf/cat XP to **0** (drops were already empty → killing a pet/wild wolf-cat now yields nothing) |
| **Mob-vs-mob bites ignored terrain** — two mobs could hit through a thin wall/door | Added the same voxel **line-of-sight raycast** the player-facing strike uses (`mobVsMobLineOfSight`) |
| `restoreMobs` accepted **any** persisted mob — a tampered v14 save could load a "pet zombie" | Restore now **rejects anything that isn't an owned ally** (mirrors the write-side `isPersistentMob`); PR-B relaxes it for residents |

**Minor (7):**
- Restored **baby pets floated** until their first tick → re-ground `position.y` after shrinking `halfHeight`.
- Holding a pet's **breeding treat no longer falls through to sit-toggle** (a declined breed can't flip sit state).
- **Sitting pet was scaled around its center**, lifting its feet → lower it so it crouches onto the ground.
- Test robustness: **unique mob ids** (so `targetId` assertions can't resolve to the attacker), persistence test uses a **real wolf**, empty-`mobs` assertion tolerates the optional field. Added tests: LOS-blocked bite, sit declines on the treat, restore drops non-pet entries.
- Docs: the MobKind checklist is **seven** exhaustive tables, not six (+ same fix in architecture.md).

I judged all ten valid (mostly quick wins) and applied them — none were the kind of stylistic nit worth declining. The type-narrowing one I addressed via CodeRabbit's own suggested alternative (restore-side validation) rather than narrowing `SavedMob`'s type, so PR-B can still persist villagers.

474	    for (let x = cx - half; x <= cx + half; x += 1) {
475	      for (let z = cz - half; z <= cz + half; z += 1) {
476	        const wall = x === cx - half || x === cx + half || z === cz - half || z === cz + half;
477	        if (!wall) continue;
478	        const isWindow = y === floorY + 1 && ((x === cx && (z === cz - half || z === cz + half)) || (z === cz && (x === cx - half || x === cx + half)));
479	        world.set(x, y, z, isWindow ? BlockId.Glass : BlockId.Brick);
480	      }
481	    }
482	  }
483	
484	  world.set(cx, floorY + 1, cz - half, BlockId.Air);
485	  world.set(cx, floorY + 2, cz - half, BlockId.Air);
486	
487	  for (let y = floorY; y <= floorY + 3; y += 1) {
488	    world.set(cx - half, y, cz - half, BlockId.Wood);
489	    world.set(cx + half, y, cz - half, BlockId.Wood);
490	    world.set(cx - half, y, cz + half, BlockId.Wood);
491	    world.set(cx + half, y, cz + half, BlockId.Wood);
492	  }
493	
494	  for (let x = cx - half - 1; x <= cx + half + 1; x += 1) {

496	  }
497	}

499	// ── Dungeons ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
500	// Small underground cobblestone rooms with pre-fillable loot chests and a mob
501	// spawner. The chest CONTENTS are not generated here (the block-diff save can't
502	// carry worldgen-placed entities), only the blocks — the engine fills chests
503	// lazily on first open. To support that, the engine re-derives the chest and
504	// spawner voxel indices on load via collectDungeonSites(), which replays this
505	// exact placement math. Two invariants keep build and derive in lockstep:
506	//   1. A dedicated PRNG seeded only from world.seed (independent of the shared
507	//      generation stream), and every dungeon draws a fixed number of values up
508	//      front so the stream stays aligned whether or not the dungeon is placed.
509	//   2. Placement validates against terrainTopY() — a seed-pure surface estimate

510	//      — never highestSolidY(), which a cave or a player edit could shift.
511	
512	type DungeonSink = { chest: (idx: number) => void; spawner: (idx: number) => void };
513	
514	const NOOP_DUNGEON_SINK: DungeonSink = { chest: () => {}, spawner: () => {} };
515	
516	/** A PRNG seeded only from the world seed, decoupled from the main gen stream. */
517	function dungeonRand(seed: number): () => number {
518	  let t = (seed ^ 0x9e3779b9) >>> 0;
519	  return () => {
520	    t += 0x6d2b79f5;
521	    let r = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), 1 | t);
522	    r ^= r + Math.imul(r ^ (r >>> 7), 61 | r);
523	    return ((r ^ (r >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
524	  };
525	}
526	
527	/**
528	 * The generation-time terrain surface at (x,z), computed purely from the seed
529	 * (mirrors the topY math in generateTerrain). Unlike highestSolidY it reads no
530	 * blocks, so it is identical at generation and at load — the property that lets
531	 * collectDungeonSites reproduce the exact dungeon layout.
532	 */
533	function terrainTopY(world: VoxelWorld, x: number, z: number, cfg: TerrainConfig): number {
534	  const biome = world.getBiome(x, z);
535	  const noise = smoothNoise2D(x, z, world.seed);
536	  const { baseHeight, noiseScale } = cfg.biomes[biome];
537	  return Math.max(5, Math.min(world.sizeY - 5, Math.floor(baseHeight + noise * noiseScale)));
538	}
539	
540	function buildDungeonRoom(world: VoxelWorld, cx: number, cz: number, floorY: number, secondChest: boolean, write: boolean, sink: DungeonSink): void {
541	  const half = 3; // 7x7 outer, 5x5x4 hollow interior
542	  if (write) {
543	    for (let y = floorY - 1; y <= floorY + 4; y += 1) {
544	      for (let x = cx - half; x <= cx + half; x += 1) {
545	        for (let z = cz - half; z <= cz + half; z += 1) {
546	          if (!world.inBounds(x, y, z)) continue;
547	          const interior = x > cx - half && x < cx + half && z > cz - half && z < cz + half && y >= floorY && y <= floorY + 3;
548	          if (interior) {
549	            world.set(x, y, z, BlockId.Air);
550	          } else {
551	            const mossy = hash2D(x * 1.7 + y * 0.9, z * 2.3 - y * 0.6) > 0.6;
552	            world.set(x, y, z, mossy ? BlockId.MossyCobblestone : BlockId.Cobblestone);
553	          }
554	        }
555	      }
556	    }
557	    world.set(cx - 2, floorY, cz - 2, BlockId.Chest);
558	    if (secondChest) world.set(cx + 2, floorY, cz + 2, BlockId.Chest);
559	    world.set(cx, floorY, cz, BlockId.Spawner);
560	  }
561	  sink.chest(world.index(cx - 2, floorY, cz - 2));
562	  if (secondChest) sink.chest(world.index(cx + 2, floorY, cz + 2));
563	  sink.spawner(world.index(cx, floorY, cz));
564	}
565	
566	function buildDungeons(world: VoxelWorld, write: boolean, sink: DungeonSink, cfg: TerrainConfig): void {
567	  const rand = dungeonRand(world.seed);
568	  const centerX = world.sizeX / 2;
569	  const centerZ = world.sizeZ / 2;
570	  for (let i = 0; i < GEN.dungeonCount; i += 1) {
571	    // Draw every random up front so the stream advances identically whether or
572	    // not this dungeon turns out to be placeable.
573	    const cx = 12 + Math.floor(rand() * (world.sizeX - 24));
574	    const cz = 12 + Math.floor(rand() * (world.sizeZ - 24));
575	    const floorRoll = rand();
576	    const secondChest = rand() < 0.6;
577	
578	    const surface = terrainTopY(world, cx, cz, cfg);
579	    const minFloor = 7;
580	    const maxFloor = surface - 7; // keep the ceiling >=3 below the surface
581	    if (maxFloor < minFloor) continue;
582	    // Keep dungeons clear of the spawn area so there's no free starter loot.
583	    if (Math.hypot(cx - centerX, cz - centerZ) < 40) continue;
584	
585	    const floorY = minFloor + Math.floor(floorRoll * (maxFloor - minFloor + 1));
586	    buildDungeonRoom(world, cx, cz, floorY, secondChest, write, sink);
587	  }
588	}
589	
590	function placeDungeons(world: VoxelWorld, cfg: TerrainConfig): void {
591	  buildDungeons(world, true, NOOP_DUNGEON_SINK, cfg);
592	}
593	
594	export type DungeonSites = { chestIndices: number[]; spawnerIndices: number[] };
595	
596	/**
597	 * Re-derives the voxel indices of every dungeon chest and spawner WITHOUT
598	 * writing blocks, by replaying buildDungeons' placement math. The engine calls
599	 * this once after regenerating the world on load to rebuild the session-only
600	 * dungeon index sets that gate lazy loot fill and spawner activation. It must be
601	 * passed the same worldType the world was generated with — dungeon depths follow
602	 * the type's terrain, so the derived indices match what placeDungeons wrote.
603	 */
604	export function collectDungeonSites(world: VoxelWorld, worldType: WorldType = "default"): DungeonSites {
605	  const chestIndices: number[] = [];
606	  const spawnerIndices: number[] = [];
607	  buildDungeons(world, false, { chest: (idx) => chestIndices.push(idx), spawner: (idx) => spawnerIndices.push(idx) }, terrainConfigFor(worldType));
608	  return { chestIndices, spawnerIndices };
```

{
  "command": "cat >> lib/world/generation.ts <<'EOF'\n\n// ── Villages ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Clusters of houses on flat, dry land. Like dungeons, the world's block diff\n// can't carry the resident villagers, so the engine re-derives each village's\n// center on load (collectVillageSites) and seeds residents there. The same two\n// invariants keep build and derive in lockstep: a dedicated PRNG seeded only from\n// world.seed, with a fixed number of draws per village; and seed-pure validation\n// via terrainTopY (never highestSolidY, which caves/edits could shift).\n\n/** Resident-spawn centers a village contributes (one per placed village). */\ntype VillageSink = (cx: number, cz: number) => void;\nconst NOOP_VILLAGE_SINK: VillageSink = () => {};\n\n/** House offsets from the village center — a tidy cross (center + four arms), spaced so 7-wide footprints don't overlap. */\nconst VILLAGE_HOUSE_OFFSETS: ReadonlyArray<readonly [number, number]> = [\n  [0, 0],\n  [9, 0],\n  [-9, 0],\n  [0, 9],\n  [0, -9],\n  [9, 9],\n  [-9, -9],\n  [9, -9],\n  [-9, 9]\n];\n\n/** A PRNG seeded only from the world seed, decoupled from the main gen and dungeon streams. */\nfunction villageRand(seed: number): () => number {\n  let t = (seed ^ 0x85ebca6b) >>> 0;\n  return () => {\n    t += 0x6d2b79f5;\n    let r = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), 1 | t);\n    r ^= r + Math.imul(r ^ (r >>> 7), 61 | r);\n    return ((r ^ (r >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;\n  };\n}\n\nfunction buildVillages(world: VoxelWorld, write: boolean, sink: VillageSink, cfg: TerrainConfig): void {\n  const rand = villageRand(world.seed);\n  const centerX = world.sizeX / 2;\n  const centerZ = world.sizeZ / 2;\n  for (let i = 0; i < GEN.villageCount; i += 1) {\n    // Draw every random up front so the stream advances identically whether or\n    // not this village turns out to be placeable.\n    const cx = 20 + Math.floor(rand() * (world.sizeX - 40));\n    const cz = 20 + Math.floor(rand() * (world.sizeZ - 40));\n\n    const surface = terrainTopY(world, cx, cz, cfg);\n    // Dry, buildable land only (above sea level, not into the sky), and clear of\n    // the spawn area so the player doesn't start inside a settlement.\n    if (surface <= cfg.seaLevel || surface >= world.sizeY - 8) continue;\n    if (Math.hypot(cx - centerX, cz - centerZ) < GEN.villageMinSpawnDistance) continue;\n\n    if (write) {\n      // placeHouse validates each spot's flatness itself and skips unsuitable\n      // ones, so a village on rougher ground simply ends up with fewer houses.\n      for (let h = 0; h < GEN.villageHouseCount; h += 1) {\n        const [ox, oz] = VILLAGE_HOUSE_OFFSETS[h];\n        placeHouse(world, cx + ox, cz + oz);\n      }\n    }\n    sink(cx, cz);\n  }\n}\n\nfunction placeVillages(world: VoxelWorld, cfg: TerrainConfig): void {\n  buildVillages(world, true, NOOP_VILLAGE_SINK, cfg);\n}\n\nexport type VillageSites = { centers: Array<{ x: number; z: number }> };\n\n/**\n * Re-derives every village's center WITHOUT writing blocks, by replaying\n * buildVillages' placement math. The engine calls this once after regenerating\n * the world on load to rebuild the session-only village sites that seed resident\n * villagers. Must be passed the same worldType the world was generated with.\n */\nexport function collectVillageSites(world: VoxelWorld, worldType: WorldType = \"default\"): VillageSites {\n  const centers: Array<{ x: number; z: number }> = [];\n  buildVillages(world, false, (x, z) => centers.push({ x, z }), terrainConfigFor(worldType));\n  return { centers };\n}\nEOF\necho \"appended village functions\"",
  "description": "Append village generation functions"
}

  "new_string": "/**\n * Seed-pure flatness gate: true when the surface under every house in the village\n * stays within villageFlatnessTolerance of the center's floor. Reads only\n * terrainTopY (no blocks), so build and derive agree on which villages exist.\n */\nfunction villageGroundFlat(world: VoxelWorld, cx: number, cz: number, baseSurface: number, cfg: TerrainConfig): boolean {\n  for (let h = 0; h < GEN.villageHouseCount; h += 1) {\n    const [ox, oz] = VILLAGE_HOUSE_OFFSETS[h];\n    if (!world.inBounds(cx + ox, baseSurface, cz + oz)) return false;\n    if (Math.abs(terrainTopY(world, cx + ox, cz + oz, cfg) - baseSurface) > GEN.villageFlatnessTolerance) return false;\n  }\n  return true;\n}\n\n/** Levels a 9×9 pad to `floorY-1` (clearing terrain bumps above, filling just below) and builds a house on it. */\nfunction buildVillageHouse(world: VoxelWorld, cx: number, cz: number, floorY: number): void {\n  const pad = 4; // house footprint half-width plus its border\n  for (let x = cx - pad; x <= cx + pad; x += 1) {\n    for (let z = cz - pad; z <= cz + pad; z += 1) {\n      if (!world.inBounds(x, floorY - 1, z)) return;\n      world.set(x, floorY - 2, z, BlockId.Dirt);\n      world.set(x, floorY - 1, z, BlockId.Grass);\n      for (let y = floorY; y <= floorY + 5; y += 1) world.set(x, y, z, BlockId.Air);\n    }\n  }\n  buildHouseShell(world, cx, cz, floorY);\n}\n\nfunction buildVillages(world: VoxelWorld, write: boolean, sink: VillageSink, cfg: TerrainConfig): void {\n  const rand = villageRand(world.seed);\n  const centerX = world.sizeX / 2;\n  const centerZ = world.sizeZ / 2;\n  for (let i = 0; i < GEN.villageCount; i += 1) {\n    // Draw every random up front so the stream advances identically whether or\n    // not this village turns out to be placeable.\n    const cx = 20 + Math.floor(rand() * (world.sizeX - 40));\n    const cz = 20 + Math.floor(rand() * (world.sizeZ - 40));\n\n    const surface = terrainTopY(world, cx, cz, cfg);\n    // Dry, buildable land only (above sea level, not into the sky), clear of the\n    // spawn area, and flat enough across the whole footprint — all seed-pure, so\n    // the record pass derives the exact same set of villages the write pass built.\n    if (surface <= cfg.seaLevel || surface >= world.sizeY - 8) continue;\n    if (Math.hypot(cx - centerX, cz - centerZ) < GEN.villageMinSpawnDistance) continue;\n    if (!villageGroundFlat(world, cx, cz, surface, cfg)) continue;\n\n    if (write) {\n      const floorY = surface + 1;\n      for (let h = 0; h < GEN.villageHouseCount; h += 1) {\n        const [ox, oz] = VILLAGE_HOUSE_OFFSETS[h];\n        buildVillageHouse(world, cx + ox, cz + oz, floorY);\n      }\n      // Cobblestone paths along the cross arms tie the houses into one settlement.\n      for (let d = -9; d <= 9; d += 1) {\n        if (world.inBounds(cx + d, floorY - 1, cz)) world.set(cx + d, floorY - 1, cz, BlockId.Cobblestone);\n        if (world.inBounds(cx, floorY - 1, cz + d)) world.set(cx, floorY - 1, cz + d, BlockId.Cobblestone);\n      }\n    }\n    sink(cx, cz);\n  }\n}"
}

8	function mulberry32(seed: number): () => number {
9	  let t = seed >>> 0;
10	  return () => {
11	    t += 0x6d2b79f5;
12	    let r = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), 1 | t);
13	    r ^= r + Math.imul(r ^ (r >>> 7), 61 | r);
14	    return ((r ^ (r >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
15	  };
16	}

  "new_string": "export function spawnVillageResidents(state: GameState, sites: Array<{ x: number; z: number }>, rng: () => number, surfaceYAt: SurfaceYAtFn): void {\n  for (const site of sites) {\n    for (let i = 0; i < GEN.villagersPerVillage; i += 1) {\n      const pos = randomLandPointNear(state.world, surfaceYAt, site.x, site.z, 8, rng, 0);\n      pushMob(state, \"villager\", false, pos.x, pos.y, pos.z, rng);\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Assigns a trade profession (round-robin) to every villager that doesn't have\n * one yet — newly seeded residents on a fresh world. Restored residents keep\n * their saved profession, so this skips them (they're not professionless).\n */\nexport function assignVillagerProfessions(state: GameState): void {\n  let next = 0;\n  for (const mob of state.mobs) {\n    if (mob.faction !== \"villager\" || mob.profession != null) continue;\n    mob.profession = PROFESSIONS[next % PROFESSIONS.length];\n    next += 1;\n  }\n}"
}

import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";
import { createEmptySlot, createSlot, ITEM_DEF_BY_ID } from "@/lib/game/items";
import { canCraft, countsById, craft } from "@/lib/game/inventory";
import { TRADES } from "@/lib/game/trades";
import type { InventorySlot } from "@/lib/game/types";

function inventory(items: Array<[string, number]>): InventorySlot[] {
  const slots = Array.from({ length: 12 }, () => createEmptySlot());
  items.forEach(([id, count], i) => {
    slots[i] = createSlot(id, count);
  });
  return slots;

{
  "file_path": "/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/engine/systems/raid.ts",
  "content": "import {\n  RAID_RADIUS,\n  RAID_REWARD_EMERALDS,\n  RAID_REWARD_XP,\n  RAID_WAVE_COUNT,\n  RAID_WAVE_DELAY_SECONDS,\n  RAID_WAVE_SIZE\n} from \"@/lib/game/config\";\nimport { hostilesSpawn } from \"@/lib/game/difficulties\";\nimport { adjustSlotCount } from \"@/lib/game/inventory\";\nimport { randomLandPointNear, type SurfaceYAtFn } from \"@/lib/game/spawn\";\nimport type { EmitGameEvent, GameState } from \"../state\";\nimport { pushMob } from \"./spawnDirector\";\nimport { awardXp } from \"./xp\";\n\nexport type RaidDeps = {\n  surfaceYAt: SurfaceYAtFn;\n  rng: () => number;\n  emit: EmitGameEvent;\n};\n\n/** Living raiders in the world. */\nfunction countRaiders(state: GameState): number {\n  return state.mobs.reduce((n, mob) => n + (mob.faction === \"raider\" ? 1 : 0), 0);\n}\n\n/** Living villagers within the raid radius of its center — once zero, the village has fallen. */\nfunction residentsNearCenter(state: GameState, center: { x: number; z: number }): number {\n  const r2 = RAID_RADIUS * RAID_RADIUS;\n  return state.mobs.reduce((n, mob) => {\n    if (mob.faction !== \"villager\") return n;\n    const dx = mob.position.x - center.x;\n    const dz = mob.position.z - center.z;\n    return n + (dx * dx + dz * dz <= r2 ? 1 : 0);\n  }, 0);\n}\n\n/**\n * Begins a raid centered on (cx, cz). Refused (returns false) when one is already\n * running or hostiles can't spawn (Peaceful). The first wave drops on the next tick.\n */\nexport function startRaid(state: GameState, cx: number, cz: number): boolean {\n  if (state.raid || !hostilesSpawn(state.difficulty)) return false;\n  state.raid = { center: { x: cx, z: cz }, wavesSpawned: 0, totalWaves: RAID_WAVE_COUNT, waveTimer: 0 };\n  return true;\n}\n\nfunction spawnWave(state: GameState, deps: RaidDeps): void {\n  const raid = state.raid;\n  if (!raid) return;\n  for (let i = 0; i < RAID_WAVE_SIZE; i += 1) {\n    const pos = randomLandPointNear(state.world, deps.surfaceYAt, raid.center.x, raid.center.z, RAID_RADIUS, deps.rng, RAID_RADIUS * 0.6);\n    pushMob(state, \"raider\", true, pos.x, pos.y, pos.z, deps.rng);\n    deps.emit({ type: \"mobSpawned\", kind: \"raider\", x: pos.x, y: pos.y, z: pos.z });\n  }\n  raid.wavesSpawned += 1;\n  deps.emit({ type: \"raidWaveStarted\", wave: raid.wavesSpawned, totalWaves: raid.totalWaves });\n}\n\n/**\n * Drives the active raid's wave state machine: spawn a wave, wait for it to be\n * cleared, then (after a delay) spawn the next, until all waves are beaten (win:\n * emeralds + XP) or every nearby villager is dead (loss). Switching to Peaceful\n * cancels it (raiders despawn via despawnHostiles).\n */\nexport function tickRaid(state: GameState, dt: number, deps: RaidDeps): void {\n  const raid = state.raid;\n  if (!raid) return;\n  if (!hostilesSpawn(state.difficulty)) {\n    state.raid = null; // Peaceful cancels the raid cleanly\n    return;\n  }\n\n  // The village fell — only checked once raiders are actually in play, so a raid\n  // can't lose on the tick before its first wave even spawns.\n  if (raid.wavesSpawned > 0 && residentsNearCenter(state, raid.center) === 0) {\n    state.raid = null;\n    deps.emit({ type: \"raidLost\" });\n    return;\n  }\n\n  if (countRaiders(state) > 0) return; // a wave is still standing\n\n  if (raid.wavesSpawned >= raid.totalWaves) {\n    // Every wave beaten — the village holds.\n    state.raid = null;\n    state.inventory = adjustSlotCount(state.inventory, \"emerald\", RAID_REWARD_EMERALDS) ?? state.inventory;\n    awardXp(state, RAID_REWARD_XP, deps.emit);\n    deps.emit({ type: \"raidWon\" });\n    return;\n  }\n\n  // Between waves: count down (the first wave starts immediately, waveTimer 0).\n  raid.waveTimer -= dt;\n  if (raid.waveTimer <= 0) {\n    spawnWave(state, deps);\n    raid.waveTimer = RAID_WAVE_DELAY_SECONDS;\n  }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { describe, expect, test } from \"bun:test\";\nimport { RAID_REWARD_EMERALDS, RAID_WAVE_COUNT, RAID_WAVE_DELAY_SECONDS, RAID_WAVE_SIZE } from \"@/lib/game/config\";\nimport { GameEngine } from \"@/lib/game/engine/GameEngine\";\nimport { createSurfaceYAt } from \"@/lib/game/spawn\";\nimport { countsById } from \"@/lib/game/inventory\";\nimport { pushMob } from \"@/lib/game/engine/systems/spawnDirector\";\nimport { startRaid, tickRaid, type RaidDeps } from \"@/lib/game/engine/systems/raid\";\nimport type { GameEvent } from \"@/lib/game/engine/state\";\n\nfunction mulberry32(seed: number): () => number {\n  let t = seed >>> 0;\n  return () => {\n    t += 0x6d2b79f5;\n    let r = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), 1 | t);\n    r ^= r + Math.imul(r ^ (r >>> 7), 61 | r);\n    return ((r ^ (r >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;\n  };\n}\n\nfunction makeEngine(): GameEngine {\n  return new GameEngine({ seed: 1337, rng: mulberry32(42), worldSize: { x: 64, y: 150, z: 64 } });\n}\n\nfunction raidDeps(e: GameEngine): { deps: RaidDeps; events: GameEvent[] } {\n  const events: GameEvent[] = [];\n  return { deps: { surfaceYAt: createSurfaceYAt(e.state.world), rng: mulberry32(7), emit: (ev) => events.push(ev) }, events };\n}\n\nconst raiders = (e: GameEngine) => e.state.mobs.filter((m) => m.faction === \"raider\").length;\n\ndescribe(\"startRaid\", () => {\n  test(\"begins a raid, and refuses a second one or one in Peaceful\", () => {\n    const e = makeEngine();\n    expect(startRaid(e.state, 30, 30)).toBe(true);\n    expect(e.state.raid?.totalWaves).toBe(RAID_WAVE_COUNT);\n    expect(startRaid(e.state, 30, 30)).toBe(false); // already running\n\n    e.state.raid = null;\n    e.state.difficulty = \"peaceful\";\n    expect(startRaid(e.state, 30, 30)).toBe(false); // Peaceful never raids\n  });\n});\n\ndescribe(\"tickRaid\", () => {\n  function seedVillager(e: GameEngine): void {\n    pushMob(e.state, \"villager\", false, 30, 30, 30, () => 0.5); // a resident at the raid center\n  }\n\n  test(\"clearing every wave wins the raid with an emerald reward\", () => {\n    const e = makeEngine();\n    e.state.mobs = [];\n    seedVillager(e);\n    startRaid(e.state, 30, 30);\n    const { deps, events } = raidDeps(e);\n\n    tickRaid(e.state, 0.1, deps); // the first wave drops immediately\n    expect(raiders(e)).toBe(RAID_WAVE_SIZE);\n    expect(events.some((ev) => ev.type === \"raidWaveStarted\" && ev.wave === 1)).toBe(true);\n\n    let guard = 0;\n    while (e.state.raid && guard++ < 50) {\n      e.state.mobs = e.state.mobs.filter((m) => m.faction !== \"raider\"); // wipe the wave\n      tickRaid(e.state, RAID_WAVE_DELAY_SECONDS + 0.1, deps); // advance past the delay → next wave or win\n    }\n\n    expect(e.state.raid).toBeNull();\n    expect(events.some((ev) => ev.type === \"raidWon\")).toBe(true);\n    expect(events.filter((ev) => ev.type === \"raidWaveStarted\")).toHaveLength(RAID_WAVE_COUNT);\n    expect(countsById(e.state.inventory).get(\"emerald\")).toBe(RAID_REWARD_EMERALDS);\n  });\n\n  test(\"the raid is lost when every nearby villager dies\", () => {\n    const e = makeEngine();\n    e.state.mobs = [];\n    seedVillager(e);\n    startRaid(e.state, 30, 30);\n    const { deps, events } = raidDeps(e);\n\n    tickRaid(e.state, 0.1, deps); // wave 1 spawns\n    e.state.mobs = e.state.mobs.filter((m) => m.faction !== \"villager\"); // the village falls\n    tickRaid(e.state, 0.1, deps);\n\n    expect(e.state.raid).toBeNull();\n    expect(events.some((ev) => ev.type === \"raidLost\")).toBe(true);\n  });\n\n  test(\"switching to Peaceful cancels an in-progress raid\", () => {\n    const e = makeEngine();\n    startRaid(e.state, 30, 30);\n    e.state.difficulty = \"peaceful\";\n    const { deps } = raidDeps(e);\n\n    tickRaid(e.state, 0.1, deps);\n    expect(e.state.raid).toBeNull();\n  });\n});\n"
}

  "new_string": "## [Unreleased]\n\n### Added\n\n- **Generated villages, villager professions & raids** (Living World, PR 2 of 2): the world is now inhabited and contested.\n  - **Villages**: clusters of houses generate on flat, dry land — terraced and built so they're actually visible (the old loose houses rarely fit natural terrain, so they barely appeared). Villager **residents** spawn and live there and **persist with the world**; villagers no longer scatter loosely (a village-less seed falls back to a few wandering ones near spawn, so trading is always available). Bumps **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9** — existing worlds of the old version reboot from their seed, and the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined — with no save-schema change for the villages themselves (residents ride the v14 `mobs` field). Villages run on their own decoupled PRNG (`villageRand`) placed last, so every other generation pass stays byte-identical to a village-less world of the same seed.\n  - **Villager professions**: each villager is a **farmer, blacksmith, librarian, or cleric** and offers only its own slice of the trade economy (a sell + a buy each), its smock tinted to its profession. Opening a villager filters the Trading recipe book to its offers and gates the craft command — you can't craft a blacksmith trade while talking to a farmer (a spoof guard on dispatch, not just the UI). Save schema bumps **v14→v15** (a resident's additive `profession` on its `SavedMob`; pre-v15 villagers load professionless and the engine assigns one).\n  - **Raids**: a craftable **Ominous Horn** (3 gold ore + 2 bone + 4 gunpowder) sounded near a village calls down **`RAID_WAVE_COUNT` (3)** waves of a new **raider** mob; clear them all for an emerald + XP reward, or — if every nearby villager dies first — the village falls. Raiders hunt villagers (and your pets defend), reusing the mob allegiance and mob-vs-mob combat from PR 1, so they needed no AI change. A raid is transient (`state.raid`, like the boss — a reload cancels it), so there's no save bump beyond the additive horn item; worldgen is unchanged (stays 9).\n- **Tameable companions & a living mob world** (Living World, PR 1 of 2):"
}

```
60:- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5 → v6 → v7 → v8 → v9 → v10 → v11 → v12 → v13 → v14.
75:`worldgenVersion` records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (`lib/game/config.ts`, currently 8) the world was generated under. This **replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump**: when the worldgen baseline changes, bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, and a world whose recorded version differs has its stale block-diffs discarded and reboots from its stored seed — per-world, with no key rename and without touching unaffected worlds.
```
