58	**Projectiles** are session-only entities (`ProjectileState` in `state.ts`, spawned via `projectiles.ts` `spawnArrow`), never serialized — like mobs. A `fromPlayer` flag is the hit filter: player arrows (the bow) hit mobs with knockback, mob arrows hit the player (armor-mitigated), and neither hits the firer. The bow, ranged skeletons, and the boss all share this one launch path. Thrown **spears** are a parallel transient entity (`ThrownSpearState`, `systems/spears.ts`) with their own gravity, swept mob collision, and terrain raycasts.
59	
60	**Endgame boss & victory.** A `"boss"` `MobKind` is summoned from a held Cursed Totem via a step in the `placeBlock` precedence (`GameEngine.trySummonBoss`, which seeds placement and refuses if a boss already exists). Defeating it (`removeMobAt`) drops a Dragon Heart, sets the session-only `state.victory`, and emits `bossDefeated`. Boss HP, player-relative bearing, horizontal block distance, and the victory flag reach React through `GameSnapshot.boss`/`victory`; the `boss` object is rebuilt only when one of its rounded visible values changes, avoiding sub-block React churn. Renderer-side hostile health bars are procedural `THREE.Sprite`s attached to each mob model and updated directly from `MobState.hp`, so ordinary mob damage does not enter the React snapshot. A new kind requires entries in all seven exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables (`MOB_TEMPLATES`, `FACTION_BY_KIND`, `MOB_DROPS`, `MOB_XP`, `CALL_INTERVALS`, `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS`, `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS`).
61	
62	**Game modes.** The four modes (`survival`/`creative`/`adventure`/`spectator`, `lib/game/gameModes.ts`) are a single `state.gameMode` axis. Systems gate on **intent predicates** rather than the raw id, so all four share one set of seams: `takesDamage` switches off the three damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts` (covering fall/void/lava/water/drown/mob/poison at once) plus hunger/regen/oxygen in `playerStats.ts`; `canEditBlocks`/`freeBuild` gate breaking and placing in `mining.ts`; `canInteract` gates the interaction commands in `dispatch`; `canFly`/`isNoclip` drive flight and the collision skip in `playerMotion.ts` (and the auto-unstuck skip in `step`); `mobsThreaten` folds into `activeHostile` in `mobAI.ts`; `usesInventory`/`takesDamage` hide HUD elements. `gameMode` rides the per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` → a v8 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`), but unlike `worldType` it's **switchable in-game** — `setGameMode` (`GameEngine.switchGameMode`) resets transient hazard timers, bars, flight, and noclip-entombment on the change. The transient `isFlying` is never serialized.
63

### lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts:330
_🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Don't reseed villagers from a villager-free v15 save.**

`!this.state.mobs.some((mob) => mob.faction === "villager")` treats “fresh / pre-village save” and “the player already lost every villager” as the same state. Saving after a village is wiped out and reloading will repopulate residents here, which breaks the new persistence contract. Gate this bootstrap on save provenance (for example, fresh world or pre-v15 save), not on the live mob list.


```diff

+    const needsVillagerBootstrap = !save || save.version < 15;
+    if (needsVillagerBootstrap && !this.state.mobs.some((mob) => mob.faction === "villager")) {
       if (this.state.villageSites.length > 0) {
         spawnVillageResidents(this.state, this.state.villageSites, this.rng, this.surfaceYAt);
       } else {
         const { x, z } = this.state.player.position;
         spawnMobGroup(this.state, { kind: "villager", hostile: false, count: 3, centerX: x, centerZ: z, radius: RENDER_RADIUS }, this.rng, this.surfaceYAt);
       }
       assignVillagerProfessions(this.state);

```




```suggestion
    // Seed each village's residents, but only when the world has no villagers yet
    // — a fresh world, or one upgraded from a pre-village save. A reload of a
    // populated world restored its residents above, so this is skipped (no double).
    const needsVillagerBootstrap = !save || save.version < 15;
    if (needsVillagerBootstrap && !this.state.mobs.some((mob) => mob.faction === "villager")) {
      if (this.state.villageSites.length > 0) {
        spawnVillageResidents(this.state, this.state.villageSites, this.rng, this.surfaceYAt);
      } else {
        // A village-less seed (rough/ocean terrain) still gets a few wandering
        // villagers near spawn so trading is never wholly unavailable.
        const { x, z } = this.state.player.position;
        spawnMobGroup(this.state, { kind: "villager", hostile: false, count: 3, centerX: x, centerZ: z, radius: RENDER_RADIUS }, this.rng, this.surfaceYAt);
      }
      // Give the freshly seeded villagers their trade professions (round-robin);
      // restored residents already carry theirs from the save.
      assignVillagerProfessions(this.state);
    }

### lib/game/engine/systems/raid.ts:18
_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Scope active-raider checks to the current raid.**

`countRaiders()` is global, but `startRaid()` can begin a new raid as soon as `state.raid` is cleared. After a failed raid leaves raiders alive, the next raid can get stuck at Line 75 because those old mobs keep the wave gate closed even if they belong to a different village. Track only raiders near the active center (or reject starting while local raiders remain).  
   


```diff
-/** Living raiders in the world. */

### lib/game/save.ts:212
_🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

**Backfill villager professions during the v14→v15 upgrade.**

This cannot stay a pure version bump with the current load path. `GameEngine` only calls `assignVillagerProfessions` inside the `!state.mobs.some((mob) => mob.faction === "villager")` branch, so a v14 save that already persisted resident villagers reloads with `profession` still missing forever. Those upgraded worlds lose the new profession-driven tinting/trade gating until the save is rewritten some other way. Either assign professions in this migration or run the backfill unconditionally after restore.

Periodic fork → upstream sync (`hutusi:main` → `davidhu0527:main`, base/head both `main`). Brings the **advancements & statistics** feature to upstream — **6 commits** since the v0.11.0 sync (#12).

## What

Adds the missing **progression meta**. After three combat/gear releases the game was content-rich but goal-poor — the only objective was "beat the Dragon Lord."

- **Statistics** — running counters: blocks mined, monsters slain, items crafted/enchanted, potions drunk, fish caught, animals bred, distance travelled, time played, deaths, jumps, villager trades.
- **Advancements** — a tight, flat set of **16**, one per major system (mine a log/stone/sliver/diamond, craft a pickaxe, craft a furnace, fire a bow, slay a hostile, defeat the Dragon Lord, breed animals, harvest wheat, catch a fish, enchant an item, drink a potion, sleep, trade with a villager). Each unlocks the moment its goal is met, with a toast + chime.

Both surface in a dedicated **`L`-key** two-tab overlay, **persist in the save and survive death** (like `xp`, unlike `effects`), and add **zero binary assets** — advancement icons reuse existing item/block sprites.

## How

- **One chokepoint.** Every gameplay event already funnels through `GameEngine.emit`; a single observer there folds each event into the stat counters and unlocks any advancement whose threshold the new stats just crossed — no per-system bookkeeping. The advancement set is a **declarative `{ stat, threshold }` registry** (`lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts`), so adding one is a one-line edit.
- A new broadly-useful **`crafted` event** drives the craft/brew/trade counters; `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS` (`lib/game/mobs.ts`) is the single source of truth for counting hostile kills.

Good thing you asked — I found a real bug, and I'll own it: **wild wolves and cats never spawn.** I added them to the mob templates and the taming/AI/persistence logic, but I forgot to add them to the initial spawn population (`spawnInitialMobs` above lists sheep/chicken/horse/cow/pig + hostiles — no wolf or cat), and nothing else spawns them. So right now there's nothing in the world to tame.

The tests didn't catch it because they construct wolves/cats directly in code, and no automated test (or manual playthrough) actually *finds* one — which is exactly the gap the manual gameplay pass I kept flagging would have caught.

## What works vs. what's broken

**Villagers — works. Here's how to find and trade:**
- Villagers live in **generated villages** — clusters of brick houses on flat, dry land (plains/desert). Villages are placed **at least 30 blocks from spawn** and are fairly sparse, so you'll usually have to **explore outward** to find one (watch the minimap; villagers are slow and don't flee).
- If a particular seed happens to generate *no* villages, the game drops **3 wandering villagers near spawn** as a fallback.
- **Right-click a villager** to open its trades (the recipe book switches to a Trading panel). Each villager has a **profession shown by its smock colour** — straw = farmer, dark grey = blacksmith, cream = librarian, purple = cleric — and offers only its own deals. The currency is the **emerald** (sell materials, then buy goods).

**Taming — the mechanic is right, but unreachable until I fix the spawn:**
- A wolf is tamed with a **bone** (from skeletons), a cat with **raw fish** (from fishing). Right-click the wild animal holding the treat — it's a **~1-in-3 chance** and the treat is eaten each try.
- …except there are no wild wolves/cats to right-click yet.

## The fix
It's tiny — add `wolf` and `cat` to the passive groups in `spawnInitialMobs` (plus a test asserting they actually spawn so this can't regress). Want me to do that now? It's a clean bug-fix commit straight to `main` (and I'd push the same one-line addition to the open upstream sync). I'd recommend it — it's what makes the whole companion feature actually playable.

## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# Fix: wild wolves & cats never spawn (companions unreachable)

## Context

The Living World epic (PRs #39/#40, merged) added tameable wolf/cat companions —
templates, taming, ally AI, and persistence all work. But **no wild wolf or cat
is ever spawned**, so there's nothing in the world to tame and the entire
companion feature is unreachable in actual play.

Root cause: `spawnInitialMobs` (`lib/game/engine/systems/spawnDirector.ts`) lists
the passive groups (sheep/chicken/horse/cow/pig) and the hostiles, but never
`wolf` or `cat`, and nothing else spawns them (`grep` for `"wolf"`/`"cat"` in the
engine finds no spawn site). The unit tests construct wolves/cats directly in
fixtures, so they passed without a mob ever needing to spawn; no test or manual
pass actually *finds* one.

## Change

**`lib/game/engine/systems/spawnDirector.ts` — `spawnInitialMobs`**: add two
entries to the `groups` array alongside the other passives (`hostile = false`,
scattered over `passiveRadius`):

```ts
["wolf", false, 4, passiveRadius],
["cat", false, 3, passiveRadius],
```

This is the same `[kind, hostile, count, radius]` tuple the existing animals use,
so they flow through the existing `spawnMobGroup` → `pushMob` path with their
`FACTION_BY_KIND` "wild" faction (flee the player, tameable). No other change is
needed — taming/AI/persistence already handle them.

## Test (regression guard)

Add to `lib/game/engine/systems/spawnDirector.test.ts` (the `spawnInitialMobs`
describe): a fresh engine's initial population contains at least one `wolf` and
one `cat`, so a future edit can't silently drop them again:

```ts
test("a fresh world seeds tameable wolves and cats", () => {
  const e = makeEngine("normal");
  expect(e.state.mobs.some((m) => m.kind === "wolf")).toBe(true);
  expect(e.state.mobs.some((m) => m.kind === "cat")).toBe(true);
});
```

(Passives spawn fine at the test's 64³ world — the existing "Peaceful seeds
passives" test relies on the same path.)

## Delivery

A **bug fix** — per AGENTS.md it commits **straight to `main`** (no feature
branch). One commit: `fix(mobs): spawn wild wolves & cats so companions are
tameable`. The open upstream sync PR **davidhu0527#13** has head `hutusi:main`,
so pushing this to `main` updates it automatically — no separate upstream action.

## Verification

- `bun test lib/game/engine/systems/spawnDirector.test.ts` — the new test passes.
- Full gate before pushing: `bun run lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`,
  `bun test`, `bun run build` green (no e2e needed — no renderer/input/shell
  change).
- Manual sanity (`bun run dev`): spawn into a world and confirm wolves/cats appear
  among the wildlife, and that right-clicking one with a **bone** (wolf) / **raw
  fish** (cat) tames it on a ~1-in-3 roll.

```

> AGENT

Fixed and committed to `main` locally (`18ae017`) — full gate green (lint, typecheck, format, **948 tests**, build).

**What was wrong:** wild wolves and cats were never spawned, so the entire companion feature was unreachable. **The fix:** added them to `spawnInitialMobs`'s passive groups (4 wolves, 3 cats), scattered with the other animals — they're now wild, flee you, and tame with a **bone** (wolf) / **raw fish** (cat) on a ~1-in-3 right-click. A `spawnDirector` test now asserts a fresh world contains both, so it can't regress.

So to answer your original question now that it works:
- **Wolves/cats** — they roam among the other wildlife near where you spawn (passive, they flee — approach slowly). Hold a bone or raw fish and right-click; eats the treat each try, ~1-in-3 to tame.
- **Villagers** — explore outward (villages are ≥30 blocks from spawn, brick houses on flat land); a village-less seed leaves 3 wandering near spawn. Right-click to trade; smock colour = profession.
